Someone keeps showing you how much they know and can do, in ways you never asked for. After a while, trying anything on your own starts to feel useless.

Safety: Take it seriously if the displays involve knowing where you are with no explanation, or appearing at places you chose to be alone. Also take it seriously if they refer to your children, home or work. Before you raise it or change any settings, check your phone and accounts for tracking. A sudden loss of access can be noticed. So get help from a domestic abuse advocate or a technology safety service.

Signs it might be this:
- They know things about your movements or plans that you did not share and cannot trace.
- The displays come right after you mention a decision, such as a move, a new job, or time with friends.
- The reach is always described in terms of what they could do about you or your plans.
- You find yourself dropping options you would otherwise have tried, and the reason is what they might find out.
- Asking how they knew gets a smile, a vague answer, or a hint that it is better not to ask.

Signs it is probably something else:
- When you ask how they knew, they explain simply and the explanation checks out.
- The information they hold is something you had told them yourself, and you had forgotten.
- They use their contacts to help with something you asked for, and not to comment on something you did not.
- The surprise appearance happens once, at a public event you both had reason to attend.
- Your plans remain yours to change, and nobody reacts to them.
- Their knowledge has a traceable and ordinary source, and they tell you what it is when asked.
- The reach is mentioned once and does not return in later disagreements.
- Your decisions go ahead and are met with interest rather than comment on what they could do about them.

## Device Access Demands

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/device-access-demands

You are expected to hand over your phone or passwords whenever asked. Saying no is treated as proof that you have something to hide.

Safety: Access demands can sit alongside stalking, or threats about what will be done with whatever is found. Warning signs include the other person knowing things you never told them. Others are apps you did not install, or fear of what happens if you change a passcode. Contact a domestic abuse advocate from a device they cannot reach. Ask how to check your phone safely for tracking software.

Signs it might be this:
- Access is treated as a condition of the relationship or the job, not something offered.
- Hesitation or refusal is read as an admission.
- The demand covers more over time, from one account to all, from occasional to continuous.
- A changed password or a deleted message is met with suspicion or anger.
- What was read is used to question you about conversations with friends, family or colleagues.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You offered the access yourself and can decline it later without a penalty.
- The openness is two-way, and they accept the same checks.
- The scope is narrow and written down, such as a work email only.
- A no was met with, at most, a question about why, and then accepted.
- The device is a child's and the access matches the child's age.
- Both people share by choice and either can stop without a penalty.

Sources:
- Freed et al. (2018). “A Stalker's Paradise” How Intimate Partner Abusers Exploit Technology. Proceedings of the 2018 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174241

## Behavior Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/behavior-control

Someone tells you what you can wear, where you can go or who you can see. They make you pay if you do not follow their rules.

Safety: Some rules are enforced with threats, damage to your things, anger that frightens you, or the loss of money, housing or contact with children. These are signs of coercive control, where rules and fear slowly take over daily life. In that case, avoid arguing directly about the rules. Contact a domestic abuse advocate or a legal aid service in private. Talk through a safety plan before you change anything about how you comply.

Signs it might be this:
- The statement is an order rather than a request, and 'no' is not an accepted answer.
- Breaking a rule leads to a punishment, such as days of silence or anger.
- The list of rules has grown over months, and keeps growing.
- You have started pre-empting the rules, dressing or acting to avoid a reaction.
- The rules apply to you and not to the person making them.

Signs it is probably something else:
- A preference is expressed once, as their own feeling, and you remain free to choose.
- Rules are mutual: each of you has the same kind of say in the other's choices.
- You can disagree with them and nothing is taken away or punished afterward.
- The rule is a shared household agreement made in a calm moment.
- It was said in a heated moment and later retracted.
- Requests are phrased as feelings and you are free to decline.
- The same latitude applies to both of you.
- Disagreement is followed by talk, not punishment.

Sources:
- Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. (Where the name comes from) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

## Punishment of Boundaries

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/punishment-of-boundaries
Also called: Punishment of Voice

You say no or ask for space, and something you value goes cold or goes missing until you take it back.

Safety: Penalties become a safety matter when they include threats, damage to your belongings, or using the children's time as a lever. Cutting off money or housing, or following and watching you after a no, count too. If a refusal brings fear, tell one trusted person or a domestic abuse advocate about the pattern before you set the next limit. Ask how to plan it safely.

Signs it might be this:
- The chill starts within hours of your no and lifts soon after you back down.
- The penalty falls on something you rely on, such as rides, childcare, money or invitations.
- Warmth returns in full when you give in, which makes the contrast stand out.
- Other people hear how unreasonable your limit was before you have spoken to them yourself.
- The cost is out of proportion to the size of what you asked.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They told you honestly that it hurts, and then did what you asked.
- The mood is brief and ordinary contact resumes without you giving anything up.
- What you lost is a direct, unavoidable result of your limit, and nobody added to it.
- They are in the middle of something large, such as grief or illness, and would have reacted to almost any change.
- They ask what the limit is for and then adjust.
- The reaction is spoken as a feeling, and no consequence follows it.
- Contact and help carry on at their usual level once the first awkward day has passed.
- They have adjusted to at least some of your limits over time.

## Boundary Testing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/boundary-testing
Also called: Boundary Testing (Disguised)

Someone keeps nudging past a line you have drawn, a little further each time. It never seems big enough to make a fuss about.

Signs it might be this:
- The same limit is crossed again after you have stated it plainly.
- Each crossing is a little larger than the one before.
- When you object, the answer is that it's small, or that you didn't mind before.
- The crossings come at moments when objecting would be awkward, such as in company.
- A nearby version of the same crossing turns up after you hold one line, like a text where a call used to be.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Once you have said where the line is, it stays put.
- They apologize when told and don't repeat it.
- The crossing happened somewhere the limit couldn't have been known.
- It is one event, and nothing bigger followed.
- They ask permission first and take no for an answer.
- The person stops when told and doesn't try the same thing again.
- The crossings come from honest uncertainty, and they ask where the line is.
- The size of the crossings stays the same or shrinks.

## Location Tracking

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/location-tracking
Also called: Stalking & Surveillance (Post-Separation), Stalking (Covert), Stalking (Overt)

Someone insists on seeing where you are at all times. If you turn your location off, or are somewhere unexpected, it leads to questions or a fight.

Safety: Treat sudden changes with care, because someone who can see your location may notice if it disappears. A person who turns up where you are, or knows places you never mentioned, is a warning sign. Tracking can also run through cars, family plans and shared accounts, as well as a single app. Speak with a domestic abuse advocate or hotline before switching anything off, from a device the other person has never used.

Signs it might be this:
- Switching sharing off leads to accusations, silence or pressure that makes you turn it back on.
- Your whereabouts are questioned after the fact, with details that show someone was watching the map.
- Only one of you is tracked.
- You have started planning routes or stops around what you could justify.
- You were told that location sharing is the price of the relationship being peaceful.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You turned it off recently and it was a non-event.
- Both of you see each other's location and use it for meeting up and collecting kids.
- The sharing was your idea or a shared one, and you still like it.
- It was set up for a particular trip or period and has an end.
- A question about where you are is answered by your reply, not by the map.
- Sharing is mutual, agreed and can be turned off.
- The reason is a specific one, such as a trip, and the arrangement ends.
- A dot on the map leads to 'did you get there okay?' and no cross-examination.

Sources:
- Freed et al. (2018). “A Stalker's Paradise” How Intimate Partner Abusers Exploit Technology. Proceedings of the 2018 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174241

## Smart-Home Coercion

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/smart-home-coercion

Devices in the home, like locks, cameras and heating, are used to watch you or keep you on edge. They are hard to prove because they mostly work as normal.

Safety: Watch for signs that someone knows where you have been, tracks your phone or controls who can enter. If you suspect it, do not search for or disable devices at once, because that can be noticed. Use a safe device to contact a domestic abuse or tech-safety service, and plan any changes with them first.

Signs it might be this:
- Odd device events follow arguments, plans of your own or time spent with certain people.
- You do not have equal access to the accounts, or you are told you do not need it.
- The other person refers to things the devices could have captured, though you did not tell them.
- A device you did not buy or agree to turns up, or one you own is linked to someone else's account.
- Resetting a device or changing a password is met with anger or followed by new problems.

Signs it is probably something else:
- A technician or manufacturer explains the fault and fixing it stops the behavior.
- Everyone in the home has the same access and knows what each device does.
- The odd events happen at random times, unrelated to anything you or anyone else did.
- The other person has no account access at all, and you have checked.
- A shared system's settings changed after a recent firmware update, and other households report the same fault.
- Everyone in the home can see the settings and accounts, and a technical reason explains the events.
- Fixing or resetting a device ends the behavior and nothing else follows.
- The person who manages the system has shown you the app and welcomes questions.

## Resource Sabotage / Sabotaging Success

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/resource-sabotage-sabotaging-success
Also called: Sabotaging Success, Resource Sabotage, Resource Consequence

The things you need to succeed keep going missing, and then the failure is blamed on you.

Safety: Cut-off money, transport, documents or phones can be part of financial or coercive control. That means control kept up through dependence and fear, especially at home. Watch for needing permission to spend, or being kept from your own accounts or papers. Also watch for fear of what happens if you ask. A financial abuse advocate or legal aid service can help you plan. Copies of important documents are safest with someone you trust.

Signs it might be this:
- The missing item is missing for you and not for people in similar positions.
- Support disappears close to a deadline, exam, interview or launch.
- Requests for the missing item meet delays or a shifting set of reasons.
- When the work falls short, nobody mentions the missing support.
- The thing withdrawn was previously available to you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Everyone in your position faces the same shortfall.
- The reason was given before the gap mattered.
- Once you raise it, the item or an alternative arrives.
- The person who withdrew it also bears the cost and says so.
- It happened once, and the person took responsibility for the knock-on effect.
- The shortage is shared and its cause is stated openly.
- Missing items are restored quickly once you flag them.
- The person acknowledges the knock-on effect when your work suffers.

## Ritualized Exhaustion

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/ritualized-exhaustion
Also called: Induced Debility

You are kept so busy and so short of sleep that you have nothing left for thinking, deciding or saying no.

Safety: Forced sleep loss and an unbroken schedule can sit alongside exploitative work or a group that rations rest. They can also be part of coercive control, which is a web of rules, checks and threats that runs your days. Watch for being woken or kept up by others, food or sleep used as a reward, punishment for refusing, and shrinking contact with outsiders. A doctor, a labor-rights service or a domestic abuse advocate can help you plan privately. Keeping dated notes somewhere the other person cannot find them helps.

Signs it might be this:
- Nobody can give you a date or a condition for when the load will ease.
- Requests for sleep or a day off are answered with doubt about your commitment.
- The demands rise after you have shown signs of objecting.
- Your errors and slowness get noted, but the hours behind them do not.
- You notice you now agree to things you would have refused when rested.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The heavy period has a named end and you can see it coming.
- The person setting the pace works the same hours and is exhausted too.
- You can refuse a task and the refusal is accepted.
- Time off is given back after a crunch.
- You chose the load and could change it without penalty.
- The pace has an end date and that date is honored.
- Rest is protected when you ask for it.
- The people setting the pace live under it too.

## Emotion Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/emotion-control

Some of your feelings are welcome and others cost you something, so you learn to show only the welcome ones, even at home.

Signs it might be this:
- The same feeling gets a cold, shaming or angry response on many different days, whatever the topic.
- Your good moods are noticed and praised while your low ones are called a phase, a mood or an act.
- You rehearse a cheerful face before walking in the door.
- A feeling you admitted when asked is quoted back at you in a later argument.
- The reaction to a mild feeling is far bigger than the feeling was.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The other person hides anger and tears too, and the rule applies to everyone equally.
- Disagreement and upset are welcome as long as they come without contempt or shouting.
- A request to pause comes with a promise to return, and they do.
- You can name a person or place where the same feeling is received without a cost.
- The sensitivity is about one subject, such as a recent death, and not about a whole range of feelings.
- The norms are stated openly, hold for everyone, and can be talked about.
- Anger or sadness is met with a request for a different time or tone, not with withdrawn warmth.
- You still have at least one place where you can show your full range.

Sources:
- Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. (Where the name comes from) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

## Moving-in-Silence

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/moving-in-silence

Big choices that change your life get made without you, and you find out afterwards, when there is nothing left to say except 'okay'.

Safety: Silent decisions become more serious when they take away your money, your home, your documents or your ability to reach other people. You may find accounts you cannot see, a lease you did not agree to or paperwork hidden from you. If so, quietly photograph or note what you can. Speak to a legal aid service or a domestic abuse advocate before raising it with anyone.

Signs it might be this:
- The decisions kept from you are the heavy ones: housing, debt, children, jobs, large purchases.
- You find out from a third party, a document or a bill, and not from the person who decided.
- When you object, you hear that it is too late, as though the lateness were your doing.
- Your say is asked for on small matters and not on matters that change how you live.
- The explanation offered is that you would have reacted badly, not that there was no time.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They told you as soon as they could and acknowledged you should have been asked.
- You had agreed ahead of time that this kind of decision could be made alone.
- The decision could still be changed, and they were willing to undo it when you objected.
- It was a one-time event, and since then they have asked about big things before acting.
- The secret was a pleasant surprise that was soon revealed.
- The decision was sudden, outside anyone's control, and explained with regret.
- You can reverse or reshape what happened, and your objection changes what follows.
- Both of you have at times acted first and told the other later, and both treat it as a lapse.

## Financial Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/financial-control
Also called: Financial Enmeshment, Economic Abuse, Economic Coercion, Financial Isolation

One person decides what money you can see, spend or earn. Access shifts with how you behave, which makes it hard to disagree or to leave.

Safety: Warning signs include being cut off from money after you disagree, or losing hold of your ID, phone or transport. Others are debts opened in your name, or being kept from work. Quietly make a note of what you know. Talk to a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service first. They can help you protect income, documents and credit. Do this before you raise any change with the other person.

Signs it might be this:
- You cannot see statements or balances, or you are told you would not understand them.
- Money for groceries, medicine or transport has to be requested, and may be refused after a disagreement.
- Your earnings are taken over, or work is discouraged or interfered with.
- Accounts, loans or signatures exist in your name that you never knowingly agreed to.
- Money comes up in arguments as something you owe or could lose.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Both of you can see every account and change the arrangement whenever you like.
- You chose the split for your own reasons and can spend your share without asking.
- A restriction is time-limited and openly agreed, such as repaying a debt you both took on.
- You have your own account or cash, and nothing is said when you use it.
- When you ask to see papers, they are shown without fuss.
- Both people can see all accounts, and the arrangement was chosen by both.
- You have money of your own that nobody comments on.
- Questions about money get answers and papers, not annoyance.

Sources:
- Adams et al. (2008). Development of the Scale of Economic Abuse. Violence Against Women. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1177/1077801208315529
- Postmus et al. (2012). Understanding Economic Abuse in the Lives of Survivors. Journal of Interpersonal Violence. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1177/0886260511421669

## Financial Dependence by Design

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/financial-dependence-by-design

Money, work and accounts are set up so that you could not support yourself if you left. Steps toward your own income or knowledge are discouraged.

Safety: Watch for money being used to control where you go, or threats to cut off housing, food or children's needs. Watch, too, for debts placed in your name without your knowledge, or fear when you ask about finances. A domestic violence advocate can plan privately with you, including how to build savings and records safely. Ask the advocate which phone and email are safe to use for that first contact.

Signs it might be this:
- Your wish for work or study is met with resistance that is out of proportion to the practical issue.
- You are unable to see statements, passwords or the household's debts.
- Your wages, benefits or documents are held by someone else.
- You could not pay rent and food for a month if the other person stopped contributing.
- Asking about money brings anger, silence or a reminder of how much they provide.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can see and use every account and know where things are kept.
- Plans for you to work or study are treated as a practical matter to solve together.
- The dependence began because of a health crisis or caregiving and both of you want it to change.
- You have your own money and a way to get at it that they know about and accept.
- Questions about money are answered plainly, even when the answers are awkward.
- Both people can see the whole financial picture and either could change the arrangement without penalty.
- Steps toward independence are met with practical help and not with obstacles.
- The reliance on one income has a plan and an end date that both people made.

## Golden Bars

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/golden-bars

You are given a good life, but it seems to depend on behaving a certain way. That good life is then used as the reason you should not complain or go.

Safety: The danger rises when comfort is linked to housing, immigration status, income or custody, so that disagreeing could mean losing them. Take note if you have no money or documents of your own. Speak to a domestic abuse advocate or a legal aid service about your position. Quietly gather copies of key papers before you change anything that someone might notice.

Signs it might be this:
- The benefits are brought up specifically when you disagree, complain or think about leaving.
- There are unspoken terms: things you have learned not to ask, say or do in case the comfort changes.
- Disagreements end with a reminder of what you owe, not what you think.
- Everything of value is in their name, or in a business or trust that you do not control.
- Praise for your situation comes from outsiders while the situation does not feel good to you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The comfort would continue if you disagreed, and you have disagreed and seen that.
- Your name is on the accounts, the lease or the contract, and you could manage without them.
- Hard conversations have happened about money and each of you kept your position.
- The terms are written, mutual and apply to both of you.
- Your unhappiness has a source that has nothing to do with the arrangement.
- Disagreements have happened and the lifestyle stayed the same afterwards.
- You hold your own savings, income or legal footing, and know where you stand.
- They encourage you to keep your own resources and routes.

## "I Know Best" Paternalism / Velvet Glove Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/i-know-best-paternalism-velvet-glove-control
Also called: Velvet Glove Control, "I Know Best" Paternalism, Using Privilege

Someone says they are acting for your good, but they do not accept your decision when you say no. They keep pushing or work around you.

Signs it might be this:
- You said no, and the topic keeps returning until you give in.
- Your decision was reversed or worked around without your being told.
- Disagreement is described as ungrateful, naive or hurtful to them.
- The warmth of the relationship seems to depend on your choosing as they would.
- You have started concealing decisions to avoid the argument.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They say their piece once and then back whatever you decide.
- You asked for their opinion first, so the advice is something you wanted.
- They can accept that you chose differently and the relationship stays warm.
- Their concern is about a specific danger and they say so plainly.
- The decision really does belong to both of you, such as joint finances, and both of you are weighing it.
- Concern is stated once and your final decision is supported afterward.
- They are open about the fact that it is their own worry, not a fact about your life.
- You can disagree without the relationship cooling.

## Enforcing Trivial Demands

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/enforcing-trivial-demands

Petty rules with no point are enforced as if they mattered enormously, and you learn to follow them to keep the peace.

Safety: Petty rules become a safety issue when missing one brings shouting, threats or damage to your things. They also do when it brings the loss of food, sleep, money or a place to live. Rules about who you contact or what you wear deserve attention too. If the reaction to a small slip frightens you, tell someone outside the home. Ask a domestic abuse advocate how to think through next steps.

Signs it might be this:
- You can't find the purpose of the rule, and asking for one produces irritation.
- The reaction to a slip is large, such as an hour's lecture or a day's silence, for something that took a second.
- New rules appear as soon as you've got the old ones right.
- Others in the household or team aren't held to them.
- The rule shifts: fine last week, wrong this week.

Signs it is probably something else:
- There is a simple reason, and once you hear it the rule makes sense.
- The same rule applies to the person who made it.
- A slip brings a reminder, and then the matter ends.
- You can suggest a different way and it's considered.
- The rule came from a shared decision.
- Rules come with reasons, or with a shrug and a willingness to drop them.
- Slips are met in proportion and then forgotten.
- The person following the rules has a say in making or changing them.

## Infantilization

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/infantilization
Also called: Helper-Helpless Dynamic

Someone talks and acts as though you can't handle adult life. They take over your jobs and decisions, and you end up feeling less able than you are.

Safety: Take extra care if you cannot see or reach your own money, ID, medication or documents. Take care too if you are told you are not allowed to decide. These can lead to loss of income, housing or independence, particularly for older adults and people with disabilities. Reach out to an advocate, adult protective services where they exist, or a legal aid service. Make copies of your key documents somewhere the other person cannot get to.

Signs it might be this:
- The assumption that you can't cope covers many areas of your life, and goes well beyond one skill.
- You have shown competence and the assumption stays the same.
- You are talked over or spoken for in front of other people.
- Your requests to do something yourself are brushed aside or met with a sigh.
- You have been shut out of money, accounts or documents that affect you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can ask for a task back and get it, with no fuss.
- The help is for a specific, unfamiliar job and ends when you are ready.
- You are included in the decision and your opinion counts.
- You and the other person split the household's jobs by agreement, and either of you can change the split.
- There is a real health reason for support, and your preferences still steer it.
- Help is offered, not imposed, and you can say 'I've got it'.
- You know where your money and papers are and have access to them.
- The arrangement can be renegotiated and has been.

## Forced Dependency

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/forced-dependency
Also called: Dependency Engineering, Dependency Installation, Device Dependency, Ecosystem Embedding

One person ends up unable to manage key parts of life alone. The knowledge or access they would need has been kept from them or made hard to get.

Safety: Pay particular attention if the other person holds your documents, phone, money or immigration papers. Pay attention too if asking for them back leads to anger or threats. Get independent advice from a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service before you ask. Planning how to get copies of your papers and a bank account of your own is often better done quietly. Do it with help.

Signs it might be this:
- Asking to be shown how to do something gets deflection, delay or mockery.
- You cannot get to your own papers, accounts or contacts without asking permission.
- When you gain a skill or a bit of independence, there is a reaction, such as sulking, criticism or a new problem.
- Reliance has increased over the years in place of decreasing.
- Practical matters you used to manage have drifted out of your hands without a conversation.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You could take over the task tomorrow and they would show you how.
- The task division matches what each of you prefers and has been discussed openly.
- Your reliance is tied to a particular event and is shrinking.
- All your documents, logins and accounts are open to you at any time.
- They are pleased, not unsettled, when you learn something new.
- The dependence has a clear reason and an end point, such as recovery from an operation.
- Requests to learn are welcomed and acted on.

## Health Sabotage

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/health-sabotage

Someone interferes with your pills, sleep, food or appointments in ways that wear you down, so you rely on them more.

Safety: Take extra care if medicines go missing. Take extra care too if you are kept awake or cut off from care when you try to make a change. The same goes if you feel physically unwell for no clear reason. A doctor, pharmacist or domestic abuse advocate can help you privately. Get medical help straight away if you feel seriously ill. Do the same if you think you have been given something you did not take knowingly.

Signs it might be this:
- Your pills, appointments or rest are disrupted most when you are making your own plans.
- The disruption falls on you and not on other people in the home.
- You lose track of a medicine that was always in the same place, and it turns up later.
- Someone is angry or mocking when you mention a doctor, therapist or treatment.
- Your health has worsened in a way that suits the other person, who seems more at ease when you are unwell.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Everyone in the household is run down by the same event, such as a baby, a move or an illness.
- The appointments you missed were hard to attend for reasons you can both name, and you worked out another way.
- Concerns about a treatment are raised once and you are supported to talk to your doctor.
- The person cannot help because of their own illness, but would if they could.
- Missed doses are explained by your own forgetfulness, and a pill organizer or alarm fixes it.
- The disruption has a clear shared cause, and the other person is working with you to fix it.
- You can still reach your doctor, medicine and rest when you need to, with some effort.
- When you raise a concern about your health, you are helped and not mocked.

## Body Autonomy Violations

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/body-autonomy-violations

Body Autonomy Violations are attempts to control another person's body, often justified by rules, care, authority or tradition. They include deciding what someone wears, eats, how they look, when they may use the bathroom, whether they may move, and what is done to their body without real consent.

Safety: Any unwanted touching, sexual pressure, withholding of food, water or medicine, or harm to a child is a serious safety matter. Contact emergency services if someone is in danger. Reach out to sexual assault, domestic abuse or child protection services, or a crisis line. For medical decisions, seek qualified medical advice, and for discrimination or legal matters, qualified legal advice. You do not have to confront the person yourself.

Signs it might be this:
- You are told what to wear, eat or how to look, and refusing leads to punishment or shame.
- Access to the bathroom, food or water depends on someone else's permission, beyond what is reasonable.
- Your 'no' about your own body is ignored or overruled.
- Rules seem to target some people's bodies more than others.
- You feel your body belongs more to the rules or the person than to you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Rules are explained, apply to everyone and have a clear safety or practical purpose.
- You can ask questions or request adjustments, and they are considered.
- Your consent is asked for and respected.
- Care for a child is age-appropriate and responsive to their growing say.
- Rules are changed when unfairness is pointed out.
- Your consent is sought and your decisions respected.
- There is a fair way to request adjustments.

## Mobility Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/mobility-control

Mobility Control is the restricting of a person's physical movement to make them comply. It includes controlling where someone may go, when they may leave, whether they have transport, and whether they can move freely in their own home, workplace or community.

Safety: Being locked in, blocked from leaving, having your documents held or being threatened if you leave are serious safety warnings. Contact emergency services if you are in danger. A domestic abuse service, crisis line or specialist service for trafficking or exploitation can help you plan safely and confidentially. Do not confront the person about the restrictions if they may react with violence. If immigration status is involved, seek qualified legal advice.

Signs it might be this:
- You need permission to leave, and saying no is not really allowed.
- Your keys, money for transport or documents are kept from you.
- You are followed, checked on or questioned whenever you go out.
- Going somewhere without permission leads to anger, threats or punishment.
- You feel unable to leave even when you want or need to.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can come and go freely, and plans are shared by choice.
- Rules on movement are applied to everyone, explained and open to question.
- Any limits relate to real safety concerns and are lifted when the concern passes.
- You can say no to sharing your plans without consequence.
- The person relaxes the requests when you say they feel restrictive.
- Rules are explained, shared and open to change.
- You have full access to your own keys, money and documents.

## Document Confiscation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/document-confiscation

Document Confiscation is when passports, identity cards, visas, work permits, birth certificates, academic certificates or other papers are taken from you, often 'for safekeeping'. Every time you ask for them back, there is a reason to wait.

Safety: Holding someone's documents can be a sign of trafficking or forced labor. If you are in danger or cannot leave, call emergency services. Contact a trafficking support line, a migrant support service, your embassy or consulate, or legal aid. Do not confront the person holding your papers. Specialist services can also advise safely on any worries about immigration status.

Signs it might be this:
- You asked for your papers and were refused or put off.
- You were not given a copy or a receipt.
- Return depends on paying a fee, finishing work or obeying a demand.
- You feel you cannot leave, travel or change jobs because of it.
- The same person holds your papers and controls your work, housing or money.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can get your papers back at any time, without conditions.
- You chose the arrangement and can end it.
- It is short-term, for a clear reason, with a receipt.
- It is an official process explained in writing, with a way to appeal.
- Nobody uses the papers to pressure you.
- Return is immediate when you ask.
- You have copies and know where the originals are.
- The arrangement was your choice and has a clear end.

## Debt Bondage

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/debt-bondage

Debt Bondage is when fees for travel, housing, training, recruitment or equipment are charged against your future wages, and the amount keeps growing faster than you can pay it off. Deductions are taken from each paycheck, new charges appear, and the balance never seems to fall.

Safety: Debt bondage can be a sign of trafficking or forced labor. If you are in danger or cannot leave, call emergency services. Contact a trafficking or forced-labor support line, a migrant support service, or legal aid for confidential advice. Do not confront the employer or agent, and do not let worries about immigration status stop you seeking help; specialist services can advise on that safely.

Signs it might be this:
- You do not know how much you owe or how it is calculated.
- New fees or fines keep appearing.
- You are told you owe more than when you started, after months of work.
- The same person controls your job, your housing and your debt.
- You are warned that leaving will bring consequences for you or your family.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The debt is written down, fixed and falling with each payment.
- You can see payslips that show all deductions.
- You can leave the job and repay in another way.
- Housing and work are separate, and you chose both freely.
- Questions about the debt are answered openly.
- The amount is written, fixed and falling.
- Deductions appear on payslips and can be questioned.
- You keep your own documents and can leave freely.

## Coerced Debt

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/coerced-debt

Coerced Debt is when loans, credit cards, contracts or bills end up in your name without your real consent. It can happen through someone using your details without asking, through pressure to sign, or through being misled about what you are signing.

Safety: Coerced debt is a form of financial abuse and can be part of wider control. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services. Contact a domestic abuse service, a financial counselor or a legal aid service for confidential help. Do not confront the person alone. Getting advice before acting can protect your safety and your money.

Signs it might be this:
- You find accounts or debts you did not know about.
- You were pressured, rushed or threatened into signing.
- You cannot see statements or know what is owed.
- Your refusal to sign leads to anger, threats or punishment.
- Collection letters arrive in your name for spending you did not do.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You agreed freely, with full information, and can see all the accounts.
- The other person accepts a no without consequences.
- Debt was shared openly and repayments are fair and transparent.
- A mistake was found and fixed together.
- You took on debt for a shared goal and still agree with the choice.
- All accounts are visible to both people and decisions are made together.
- Refusals are respected.
- Any mistake is acknowledged and put right.

## Children as Leverage

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/children-as-leverage
Also called: Children as Collateral Consequence

Children as Leverage is the use of a child's wellbeing, access or future as a tool to control an adult. The adult is made to feel that the child will suffer unless they comply, stay quiet, give something up or stay in a situation.

Safety: Threats to take, harm or not return children, or any risk to a child's safety, are serious. Contact emergency services if a child or adult is in danger. A domestic abuse service, child protection service or crisis line can help you plan safely, and qualified legal advice is important for custody or contact matters. Do not confront someone who has been threatening; seek specialist help before acting.

Signs it might be this:
- You are told you will lose contact with your children if you leave, complain or say no.
- A child's support is presented as depending on your agreement or silence.
- Your children are asked to pass messages, report on you or persuade you.
- Every disagreement turns into a warning about what will happen to the children.
- The person's concern for the child appears only when they want something from you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Concerns about the child are raised calmly, with a focus on the child's needs and fair options.
- You are given clear information and a route to disagree or appeal.
- The other adult supports your relationship with the children.
- The children are kept out of adult disputes.
- Discussions stay focused on the child's needs and offer real choices.
- You are given information about your rights and options.
- The other adult keeps children out of the conflict.

Sources:
- Spearman et al. (2022). Post‐separation abuse: A concept analysis. Journal of Advanced Nursing. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.15310

## Enmeshment

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/enmeshment

Enmeshment is a family-systems idea for when the line between two people's feelings, choices and identities becomes blurred or dissolved. Your moods, decisions and successes are treated as belonging to someone else, often a parent, partner or close relative.

Signs it might be this:
- Your choices are taken personally as a rejection.
- You feel guilty for keeping anything private.
- You are responsible for managing the other person's moods.
- You struggle to say what you want without checking their reaction first.
- Independence, such as moving out or choosing a different path, is treated as betrayal.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can disagree and still feel loved.
- Privacy is respected.
- The other person has their own life and interests.
- Your choices are supported even when they are not what they would choose.
- Closeness feels freely chosen on both sides.
- Disagreements are accepted and talked through.
- Privacy and separate friendships are respected.
- The other person has their own support and interests.

## Financial Enmeshment

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/financial-enmeshment

Financial Enmeshment is tangling finances together so that separating becomes catastrophic. It can happen between partners, within families, in businesses, in groups and between people and institutions.

Safety: Money control can be part of domestic abuse or coercive control. If you are afraid, contact a specialist domestic abuse service or, in danger, emergency services. If you suspect debts in your name or forced financial control, seek qualified legal or debt advice. If your job, housing and immigration status are all tied to the same person or employer, or your documents are being held, contact a specialist support or anti-trafficking service, or qualified immigration advice. Plan safely before changing accounts, because sudden moves can raise risk.

Signs it might be this:
- You were rushed to sign before you could read or get advice.
- You do not know the full picture of shared debts, assets or accounts.
- Leaving would leave you with debt, no home or no income, while the other person would be fine.
- Money is used in arguments: 'You can't afford to leave' or 'You'd lose everything.'
- New links keep being added whenever you seem to be pulling away.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Both of you have equal access to information and accounts.
- Agreements were made slowly, openly and with advice.
- There is a clear, fair way to separate finances if needed.
- Money is not raised as a reason to stay.
- You each keep some independent money and credit.
- Both people have full access and an equal say.
- There is a fair, agreed plan for what happens if you separate.
- You can get independent advice without being discouraged.

## Harm to Pets or Property

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/harm-to-pets-or-property

Harm to Pets or Property is when belongings are destroyed, or a pet is hurt or threatened, as a warning about what could happen next. The damage often targets things that matter to you: a phone, a laptop, a gift, your work tools, or an animal you love.

Safety: Treat harm to pets or property as a warning sign. If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services. For planning, contact a domestic violence or abuse service, a crisis line, or an advocate. Do not confront the person or try to recover items alone; police or legal advice can help with that. Specialist services can also help arrange safety for pets.

Signs it might be this:
- Damage happens soon after you disagree, say no or talk about leaving.
- The things destroyed are the ones you value most or need most.
- A pet is harmed, frightened or threatened as a way of upsetting you.
- You are told it was your fault for making them angry.
- You find yourself hiding belongings or the pet to keep them safe.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Damage was clearly accidental, is owned, and is repaired or replaced.
- It is not linked to conflict and does not repeat.
- There is no threat or message attached.
- Both people treat the loss with care and talk about it calmly.
- A pet's injury has an ordinary cause and is treated quickly.
- It happened once, by accident, and was fully owned and put right.
- There is no link to conflict and no threat attached.
- You feel safe, and the other person is open to getting help with anger.

Sources:
- Ascione (1997). Battered Women's Reports of Their Partners' and Their Children's Cruelty to Animals. Journal of Emotional Abuse. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1300/J135v01n01_06

## Reproductive Coercion

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/reproductive-coercion

Someone ties your job, money, home or place in the family to what you decide about having children. They keep pressing after you have answered.

Safety: Pressure about pregnancy can sit alongside violence, or threats to money, housing, children or immigration status. It can come with coercive control, which is a steady pattern of rules and threats that narrows your choices. Pregnancy can also be a time when abuse begins or worsens. Warning signs include controlled contraception or appointments, being watched at clinics, and threats tied to your answer. A domestic abuse hotline or clinic can talk privately. Ask about safe ways to reach them from a phone or device the other person cannot see.

Signs it might be this:
- Money, housing or work is mentioned in the same breath as your decision.
- The question is raised again right after you have answered it.
- Other people are lined up to press you.
- You have been told that your place in the family depends on it.
- Your access to contraception, appointments or your own records has become something you must account for.

Signs it is probably something else:
- A wish is stated and then your answer is accepted.
- Your income, home and standing do not change with your answer.
- The pressure is one conversation and both sides are open.
- Medical advice is given in full and the decision is left to you.
- Everyone at the workplace is under the same stated policy.
- Support continues whichever way you decide.
- Medical and practical information is shared openly, with the choice left to you.

Sources:
- Miller et al. (2010). Pregnancy coercion, intimate partner violence and unintended pregnancy. Contraception. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1016/j.contraception.2009.12.004

## Arbitrary Authority

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/arbitrary-authority
Also called: Effort-Outcome Mismatch, Uncontrollable Outcomes

Arbitrary Authority is when decisions that affect you follow no stated rule, so nothing you do reliably changes the outcome. The same effort is praised one day and rejected the next.

Signs it might be this:
- You have tried several ways of meeting the expectation and none reliably works.
- Asking 'what would make this a yes?' gets no answer, or a different answer each time.
- Others in the same position see the same unpredictability and have stopped asking.
- Outcomes seem to depend on whether you are in favor that week.
- When you point to an earlier decision, you are told that does not matter now.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The criteria are written down somewhere, even if they are hard to meet.
- The decider explains the difference between two outcomes when asked.
- The changes follow new information or a stated change in policy.
- The person admits they were inconsistent and works to be steadier.
- Your sense of randomness comes from one surprising result rather than a run of them.
- The decider is willing to set out criteria when asked, and sticks to them.
- Unclear decisions can be reviewed by someone else.
- Inconsistency is admitted and corrected.

## Strategic Chaos / Crisis Manufacturing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/strategic-chaos-crisis-manufacturing
Also called: Strategic Chaos

Strategic Chaos, also called Crisis Manufacturing, is a pattern of constant emergencies that keeps people reacting so they never get the time or calm to think ahead. Plans change at short notice, new urgent problems arrive one after another and every week seems to bring something that must be dealt with right now.

Safety: If the chaos is part of a wider pattern of control at home, involves threats, sudden money problems created by someone else, or danger to you or children, it is a safety matter. Contact emergency services if anyone is in immediate danger, and reach out to a domestic abuse or crisis support line. Plan any changes with specialist support rather than announcing them to the person.

Signs it might be this:
- You can rarely remember a week without some sudden urgent matter.
- Many of the crises trace back to one person or office.
- Whenever you try to raise a longer-term issue, a new emergency takes over.
- Things calm down when the person is away, and the turmoil returns when they come back.
- You are blamed for not being prepared for changes no one could have planned around.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The causes of the disruption are outside anyone's control and openly explained.
- The person helps you plan, gives warning where they can and apologizes when they cannot.
- Periods of crisis are followed by periods of stability.
- You are able to raise long-term concerns and they are taken up.
- The person responds to feedback by giving more notice and fewer sudden changes.
- You can see real external causes for the disruption.
- There is room to discuss and plan, even if things are busy.

## Collective Punishment

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/collective-punishment
Also called: Collective Consequence, Incident Identification Without Individual Accountability

Collective Punishment is when a whole group pays for something one person did, or for something no one is named for. A class loses a break, a team loses a bonus, a household loses a privilege, or an online group is locked, until 'someone owns up'.

Safety: If group blame is turning into bullying, threats or physical harm, safety comes first. Tell a trusted adult, a safeguarding lead, a supervisor or someone outside the group. Call emergency services if anyone is in immediate danger. Children should not be expected to sort this out alone.

Signs it might be this:
- You lose something for an act you had no part in.
- The penalty ends only when the group hands over a name.
- Others in the group start blaming, watching or pressuring one person.
- Whoever is in charge makes little effort to find out what actually happened.
- The group is told 'you did this to yourselves' when most did nothing.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The change is a safety step that would happen anyway, explained without blame.
- The person in charge investigates and holds only the responsible person to account.
- The whole group really did share the act.
- It is a one-off pause while facts are gathered, and it ends without needing a name.
- People are invited to share concerns privately, without pressure on the group.
- The change is explained as safety and lifted when the risk is gone.
- The innocent are not asked to identify or pressure anyone.
- A fair process finds out what happened.

## Fear Installation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/fear-installation
Also called: Anxiety Induction

Fear Installation is the slow building of a dread that stays in the background of daily life. The consequences for getting something wrong are made unpredictable.

Safety: Living in dread is serious in itself. If the vague warnings point to harm to you, your children or anyone else, or come with control over money, movement or contact, treat it as a safety matter. Do not test or challenge the person. Contact a domestic abuse helpline or specialist support service to plan safely, and call emergency services if you are in immediate danger.

Signs it might be this:
- You cannot predict how they will react to ordinary things, and the not-knowing itself feels like the point.
- Threats stay vague, and asking what exactly would happen gets a shrug, a smile or more vagueness.
- You notice you feel relief when they leave the room, and tension in your body when you hear them arrive.
- Old punishments are mentioned again without reason, as if to keep them fresh.
- Others around you also tiptoe, rehearse what to say, or hide small mistakes.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Consequences are stated ahead of time and applied the same way each time.
- When you ask what would happen, you get a straight answer you could plan around.
- The person's reactions vary because they are under stress, and they say so and try to steady things.
- Your worry is mostly about outside events, such as money or health, and no one is using it against you.
- It was one frightening moment that was talked through and has not been repeated.
- The person notices the effect of their reactions and works to be steadier and clearer.
- Rules and consequences can be asked about and are explained plainly.
- The fear fades once a hard period passes and does not get topped up.

## Institutional Capture

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/institutional-capture
Also called: System Recruitment

Institutional Capture is when the place you would normally turn to for help has already been brought onto the other side. An oversight body, a referee, a complaints office or a helping service may be influenced, or outside structures such as employers, landlords or officials may be lined up to enforce one side's wishes.

Safety: If outside bodies are being used against you around your children, housing, immigration status or safety, get qualified legal advice early, before responding to official contact where you can. A domestic abuse service or legal aid service can help you find independent routes. If you are in danger, call emergency services.

Signs it might be this:
- Each body you approach seems to have already heard a version of events from the other side.
- Your complaint reaches the person it is about before it is investigated.
- Officials or services contact you repeatedly about matters that turn out to be unfounded.
- The person boasts of knowing the people who would judge any complaint.
- Decision-makers refuse to declare a personal connection to the person involved.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The body you approached heard both sides, explained its reasons and offered a route of appeal.
- The other person contacted a service once, for a reason that made sense, and it was resolved.
- Connections between people are declared openly, and someone without a connection makes the decision.
- You learn the service contacted the other side because it is a normal step, not a favor.
- Your sense that everyone is aligned comes from one bad outcome, not a pattern.
- Conflicts of interest are declared and handled by passing the matter to someone else.
- You can reach an independent route that has no tie to the other side.
- Outside contacts were made once, in good faith, and stopped when resolved.

Sources:
- Stigler (1971). The Theory of Economic Regulation. The Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science. (Research) https://doi.org/10.2307/3003160

## Status Threats

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/status-threats

Status Threats are when your visa, residency, enrollment, work permit or legal status, or that of your family, is used as a threat. The message is: comply, stay quiet or do what you are told, or you could be reported, removed, expelled or deported.

Safety: Threats about immigration or legal status can be part of serious abuse or exploitation. If you are in danger, call emergency services. Get independent immigration or legal advice from a qualified adviser; what options exist for people facing crime or abuse depends on where you are, and an adviser can explain them. A domestic abuse service, trafficking support line or migrant support service can help confidentially.

Signs it might be this:
- Talk of your status comes up whenever you disagree or say no.
- You are told you will be reported if you complain.
- The person claims power over your status that they may not have.
- Threats include your family members.
- You stay in a harmful situation because of fear about your status.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The information is neutral, accurate and offered to help you.
- It is given in writing, with sources and a way to get advice.
- It is not tied to a demand.
- The person encourages you to check with an independent adviser.
- It is a routine reminder of a real deadline.
- The information is accurate, neutral and not tied to a demand.
- You are encouraged to get independent advice.
- There is no link to complaints or refusals.

## Legal Abuse

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/legal-abuse
Also called: Legal Abuse (Post-Separation), SLAPP, Silencing Litigation, paper abuse, litigation abuse, vexatious litigation

After a split, someone keeps taking the other person back to court. The filings look normal one by one, yet the cost in money and nerves becomes the harm.

Safety: Concern grows when filings sit alongside threats or danger to a child. It also grows with the chance of losing your home, income or custody time at the next hearing. Courts also hear true accounts of danger, so a filing is not proof of abuse. Bring the full file to a family law attorney or legal aid advocate. Ask what limits or protections your court offers.

Signs it might be this:
- The same issues come back in new papers with nothing that has changed.
- Filing dates cluster around events in your life.
- You spend more responding than the disputed amount or issue is worth.
- Several filings have been declined or dismissed, and new ones follow.
- Offers to settle are refused, then the matter returns later in another form.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Each filing cites a new fact, such as a new job, a move or a school change.
- Courts have granted at least some of the requests.
- Your own lawyer says the volume is routine for cases like yours.
- The timeline follows deadlines the court itself set.
- The matters in dispute are real, large and unresolved, like a pension or a relocation.
- The court has treated each request as serious and mostly granted it.
- The filings are spread out and tied to real changes.
- Both sides are filing, and both sides have lawyers.

Sources:
- Miller and Smolter (2011). “Paper Abuse”: When All Else Fails, Batterers Use Procedural Stalking. Violence Against Women. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1177/1077801211407290
- Gutowski and Goodman (2022). Coercive Control in the Courtroom: the Legal Abuse Scale (LAS). Journal of Family Violence. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1007/s10896-022-00408-3
- Spearman et al. (2022). Post‐separation abuse: A concept analysis. Journal of Advanced Nursing. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.15310

## Monitoring & Surveillance

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/monitoring-surveillance

Someone expects to see your phone, your messages and your whereabouts on demand. Nothing you show them ever makes the checking stop.

Safety: Watch for checking that comes with anger, threats, or knowing things you never told them. If you think your phone, email or car is being watched, assume the watcher may see what you do on it. That includes searches for help. Reach a domestic abuse hotline or advocate from a library computer, a friend's phone or a work device. Ask them how to check your devices safely before you change anything.

Signs it might be this:
- Declining to hand something over leads to accusation, anger or days of silence.
- The checking started small and has widened to more apps, more hours and more people.
- You have noticed signs that your accounts or devices were opened without your say-so.
- Showing the evidence once does not end the question; it only prompts the next one.
- You have started deleting harmless messages or avoiding contacts to stay out of arguments.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Both of you share things openly, and either can say no without a penalty.
- The request was a single one, tied to a specific scare, and has not come back.
- The access is mutual: you can look at theirs as freely as they look at yours.
- The checking has an agreed end date and a stated reason, and it ends.
- The person accepts your answer and moves on once you have given it.
- The checking is open, mutual and can be stopped by either person.
- Worry is spoken about as a feeling, and reassurance seems to help.
- Declining a request leads to a conversation, not a punishment.

Sources:
- Evan Stark (2007). Coercive Control. (Research) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL2982769W

## Response-Time Policing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/response-time-policing

Someone treats a slow reply as an offense, so you feel you must stay reachable and explain every gap.

Signs it might be this:
- A late reply is followed by a demand for an account of where you were and who with.
- Your own long silences from them are met with no questions.
- The expected reply time keeps shortening over weeks.
- Explaining does not settle it, because a new gap soon draws the same charge.
- You have started to reply from places and times where you would not choose to, such as the bathroom or a meeting.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You both agreed to the check-in rule and it applies equally.
- A missed message prompts a single worried question rather than a demand.
- The urgency comes from a real situation, such as a sick relative or a shared deadline.
- They tell you what they are feeling instead of asking you to account for yourself.
- They accept 'I was busy' without pressing further.
- The expectation is shared, written down or spoken, and applies in both directions.
- A slow reply gets a short, warm check-in and nothing more.
- The person can say what they are feeling and let you explain later without a trial.

## Interrogation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/interrogation

Instead of asking, someone demands that you explain yourself right now, and each answer only leads to another question.

Safety: Questioning moves toward danger when it goes on for hours. It also does when it blocks you from leaving the room, or includes searching your phone or belongings. The same is true if it ends in shouting, threats or physical intimidation. If you fear what happens when you decline to answer, talk privately with a domestic abuse advocate first.

Signs it might be this:
- Questions are phrased as orders or arrive in quick succession.
- 'I don't want to talk about it right now' is treated as an admission.
- You find yourself answering questions you do not think the other person has a right to ask.
- The same ground is covered again and again with slight variations to catch a slip.
- The questions come from a position of assumed guilt, not curiosity.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can say 'I need a minute' and be given one.
- The person listens to your answer rather than preparing the next question.
- The context is formal and both sides know the rules, such as a legal or medical interview.
- They also answer questions about themselves with similar openness.
- The tone is curious and the question can be dropped without fallout.
- The question can be put off, and the person returns to it calmly later.
- You are given the same freedom to ask them the same sort of questions.
- The context is formal and has clear limits, such as a set meeting time.

## Time Theft

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/time-theft

Your time keeps being used up or wasted by someone who guards their own time carefully, and no one acknowledges what it costs you.

Signs it might be this:
- The lateness or cancellations land on you far more often than on others in their life.
- They arrive on time for people and events that matter to them.
- You are expected to take whatever time they give with no warning, and complaints are met with mockery.
- They know the cost to you, for example childcare or a missed shift, and carry on.
- Your own time commitments are called unimportant in comparison to theirs.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They tell you early when they are running late and offer an alternative.
- The pattern is the same with everyone in their life.
- It is a short phase linked to a new job, new baby or illness.
- When you raise it, they adjust within a few weeks.
- You both bend around each other's time about equally.
- They notice and say sorry before you do, and take steps to avoid the next time.
- Their lateness has a clear cause that they are working on.
- The give and take of schedules is roughly even over the months.

## Time Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/time-control

Time Control is the dictating of how a person spends their hours so that little or no time is left for their own thought, rest or choices. Every part of the day is filled with required tasks, meetings, check-ins, duties or activities set by someone else.

Safety: If someone is controlling your time alongside checking your location, limiting your money or contacts, or threatening you, this may be part of coercive control. Contact emergency services if you are in danger, and a domestic abuse or crisis line for confidential help. If a child's time is being controlled in ways that harm their health or schooling, speak with a child protection or family support service.

Signs it might be this:
- You cannot remember the last time you had a few hours to spend however you liked.
- Plans you make for yourself are regularly overridden by new demands.
- You feel you must explain or justify any time spent away from required duties.
- Taking a break leads to criticism, guilt or a new task.
- The schedule is set by one person, and you have no say in changing it.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You helped plan the schedule and can change it.
- Busy times are balanced by protected rest.
- Your requests for time off are respected without penalty.
- The demands come from a temporary, shared goal that everyone agreed to.
- The person makes room for your time once you point out the problem.
- You have regular, protected periods that are yours.
- The pressure comes from circumstances that everyone is working to change.

## Controlled Communication

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/controlled-communication
Also called: Communication Chain Restriction, Constraining Verbal Expression, Vocal Regulation

Controlled Communication is the dictating of how, when and whether a person may speak. It can mean rules about who you may talk to, what you may say, when you may raise topics and through which channels.

Safety: If someone is checking your phone, controlling who you can contact, or stopping you from reaching family, professionals or emergency services, this is a serious warning sign of coercive control. Contact emergency services if you are in danger, and a domestic abuse or crisis line using a safe device. If you are being kept from speaking up about abuse, harm to a child or exploitation, specialist support services can help confidentially. Do not challenge a controlling person directly if it may make you less safe.

Signs it might be this:
- You need permission to speak, or are regularly told when and how you may talk.
- Your messages to others are read, filtered or blocked.
- Certain topics are off limits, and raising them brings anger or punishment.
- You are told to route all concerns through one person, who never passes them on.
- You find yourself checking with someone before saying anything.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Communication rules are explained, fair and open to change.
- You can reach outside support freely.
- Concerns raised through channels are heard and answered.
- Requests to pause a conversation are followed by a real return to it.
- Rules relax when you say they feel restrictive.
- There are multiple ways to raise concerns.
- Your outside contacts are not checked or limited.

## Sleep Deprivation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/sleep-deprivation

Sleep Deprivation as a tactic is the repeated disruption of a person's rest, so that they are too tired to think clearly, hold firm or resist. It can mean waking someone at night for arguments or demands, keeping them up with noise or tasks, scheduling that leaves no real time for sleep, or making rest feel unsafe or forbidden.

Safety: If you are being kept awake as part of threats, intimidation, control or abuse, or if exhaustion is putting you or children at risk, contact emergency services if you are in danger and a domestic abuse or crisis line for confidential help. See a doctor about the health effects of long-term sleep loss. Do not stay in a late-night confrontation with someone who is becoming threatening; leave if safe and seek help.

Signs it might be this:
- Serious conversations or conflicts often start just as you are trying to sleep.
- You are woken repeatedly, and asking for rest is ignored or mocked.
- You are pressured to agree to things late at night when you are too tired to think.
- You feel you are not allowed to sleep until someone else decides.
- Your rest improves noticeably when the person or setting is not present.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The disruption has a clear cause no one controls, and others try to help you rest.
- Your request for quiet or sleep is respected.
- Late-night talks are rare and mutual, and you can stop them.
- Your schedule is busy but you can and do adjust it.
- The person adjusts once they understand how it affects you.
- There are practical reasons for the disruption and you are working on them together.
- You can rest when you choose without penalty.

## Choice Restriction

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/choice-restriction
Also called: Choice Architecture Manipulation, Bounded Choice, Reflexive Control, Coercive Framing, Institutional Adoption, Token Autonomy, Token Autonomy / Coercive Framing

Your options get closed off or made to look unworkable, one at a time. In the end, the choice someone else would prefer is the only one left.

Safety: The picture changes when the closed options involve money, housing, documents, medical care or contact with other people. It matters most when the person closing them is the one who controls those things. Watch for being told you could not manage elsewhere, or being unable to see accounts or papers. Speak with a domestic abuse advocate or legal aid service before changing anything, and plan any change privately.

Signs it might be this:
- Each time you name another possibility there is a reason it will not work, and the reasons all point the same way.
- The person describing your options also controls what you would need to check them. That includes the money, paperwork, schedule or information.
- Options you would normally consider have disappeared without any conversation about removing them.
- Looking into an alternative on your own is met with irritation, or you find it was more open than you were told.
- The outcome that is left happens to suit the person doing the narrowing.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can look up alternatives yourself and the other person is happy for you to do it.
- The options that are gone were closed by a landlord, bank, rule or deadline that neither of you controls.
- When you pick the option they like less, they help you carry it out.
- They set out the trade-offs for every option, including the ones they like least.
- Checking shows the other options really are unworkable for reasons you can verify.
- The limits come from a source you can check, such as a published rule or price list.
- You can freely ask others for advice and the answer is not met with displeasure.
- When you do pick differently, nothing about your life gets harder.

## Role Assignment

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/role-assignment
Also called: Identification as Identity Assignment, Identity Narrowing, Role Confinement

Role Assignment is the fixing of an identity on a person that then shapes how they are expected to act and how they are treated. Labels such as 'the smart one', 'the difficult one', 'the carer' or 'the troublemaker' get attached early, and the person finds it hard to step outside them.

Safety: If a role is being used to justify harm, for example a child made responsible for adults' care or safety, or blamed and punished for family troubles, contact a child protection service, a trusted adult or a support line. If a label is affecting access to education, work or services in a way you cannot challenge, independent or legal advice may help. Contact emergency services if anyone is in danger.

Signs it might be this:
- You have been given a label you never chose, and it follows you everywhere.
- When you act differently, people say 'that's not like you' or push you back into the role.
- Opportunities are offered or denied based on the label rather than what you can do.
- Siblings, classmates or colleagues each seem to have fixed roles that rarely change.
- You feel you cannot be seen as anything other than your role.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The description fits and you are happy with it, and others accept when it changes.
- Groupings are reviewed and you can move between them.
- People respond with interest when you try something new.
- You chose the role and can put it down.
- People update their view of you when you show them something new.
- There is a clear, fair way to move out of a category.
- The role is one of many ways you are seen.

## Maternal Gatekeeping

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/maternal-gatekeeping

One parent keeps correcting or redoing how the other cares for the child. The other parent gives up and does less, which then seems to prove the point.

Signs it might be this:
- Tasks on which there is no single right way are corrected or redone most times they are done.
- The other caregiver has said they have stopped doing a task because it just gets redone.
- The corrections come in front of the child, family or friends.
- Access to the child is arranged around the gatekeeper's approval and rules are changed after the fact.
- A request to share more of the care meets reasons that never run out.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The parent hands over the task and leaves, even if they would have done it differently.
- The corrections are about things that affect safety and stop once the other caregiver knows them.
- Both caregivers criticize each other's methods about equally, and also accept it.
- The other caregiver has asked for the corrections or the checklist.
- The one who corrects is also teaching, and hands over more as skill grows.
- The corrector steps back once the other caregiver has shown they can do the task safely.
- Both caregivers feel their style is wanted and the child is at ease with both.
- Differences in method are discussed with curiosity instead of being fixed on the spot.

Sources:
- Allen and Hawkins (1999). Maternal Gatekeeping: Mothers' Beliefs and Behaviors That Inhibit Greater Father Involvement in Family Work. Journal of Marriage and the Family. (Where the name comes from) https://doi.org/10.2307/353894

## Performance Monitoring

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/performance-monitoring
Also called: Compliance Infrastructure

Performance Monitoring as a tactic is constant evaluation that keeps a person on edge, always aware of being watched and scored. Every task, behavior or moment is measured, logged or commented on, so the person cannot relax or act without thinking about how it will look.

Safety: If someone is checking your phone, messages, location or private life without your agreement, especially alongside threats, anger or isolation, this may be part of coercive control. Contact emergency services if you are in danger, and a domestic abuse or crisis line for confidential support. If the monitoring is affecting your mental health, talk with a doctor or counselor.

Signs it might be this:
- You feel watched and judged almost all the time.
- Small things are recorded or commented on, even when they do not matter.
- Measures change, or more are added, without explanation.
- Evaluation rarely comes with support or a way to improve.
- You are afraid to make any mistake, because it will be noted.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Monitoring is agreed, explained and limited to what is needed.
- Feedback is balanced and leads to help.
- You can discuss and question the measures.
- There is time when you are not being evaluated.
- Monitoring is reduced when you show you can work independently.
- Measures are clear, fair and discussed with you.
- Feedback includes what is going well and how to grow.

## Strategic Timing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/strategic-timing

Strategic Timing is when damaging news, a new demand or sudden pressure lands just before an important moment, so there is no time to check it, think it through or answer well. It might be a criticism the night before a big presentation, an ultimatum as you are leaving for a trip, a fee change announced during exams, or a family conflict raised on the morning of a wedding.

Signs it might be this:
- The same person's hard news keeps arriving just before your important days.
- They knew about your event and still chose that moment, with no reason it could not wait.
