- Questions and objections get a hearing, even if they are unwelcome.
- Asking for outside advice is tolerated, and you can name the problem in your own words.

## Intermittent Reinforcement / Push-Pull

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/intermittent-reinforcement-push-pull
Also called: Intermittent Reinforcement, Push-Pull, Emotional Bait-and-Switch, Intermittent Availability, Occasional Indulgences, Proximity Control, Push-Pull / Rubberbanding, Push-Pull Cycling, Variable Ratio Reinforcement, Variable Reward Scheduling

Someone is very close, then suddenly distant, then close again. You end up spending your energy trying to get back to the good part.

Signs it might be this:
- The cool phases start soon after a moment of real closeness, such as an intimate talk or a weekend away.
- Warmth returns in step with your pulling back, not in step with anything happening in their life.
- You can tell the day's mood from the first message, and you plan your own week around it.
- Asking what changed gets 'nothing' or 'you're overthinking', and the cycle begins again.
- You have been through at least three or four full swings, not one.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The quiet spells line up with something you can see, such as a work deadline or a family event.
- They tell you ahead of time: 'I'll be off my phone this week, I'll call Sunday.' And they call.
- The swings are small, and both of you move through them with no one chasing.
- When you name the gap, they explain it and the next one is shorter or better flagged.
- You are the one who tends to go cold, and they are simply responding to that.
- They name their own pattern and say what they are doing about it, such as asking for notice before they go quiet.
- The cool phases are short and the closeness comes back without you chasing.
- You can tell them it unsettles you and they are curious about that, not irritated.

Sources:
- Charles B. Ferster (1957). Schedules of Reinforcement. (Research) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL6445502W

## Hoovering / Relief Bait

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/hoovering-relief-bait
Also called: Relief Bait, Hoovering, Hoovering (Post-Discard), Hoovering (Replacement Phase), Periodic Reinforcement of the Ideal, Zombieing

After you pull away or break up, they reach out with promises, apologies or emergencies. You get drawn back, and the old pattern starts again.

Safety: Repeated unwanted contact after a breakup can slide into stalking. Threats, showing up where you live or work, or messages that mention hurting themselves or you are all danger signals. Save every message, tell someone you trust, and contact a domestic violence advocate or the police if you feel unsafe.

Signs it might be this:
- The messages begin soon after you stopped replying, as if timed to the distance.
- A no is followed by a new approach through a different route: another number, a friend, a gift to your work.
- The promise is about feelings and future, with few concrete steps you can check.
- After you return, the earlier problems come back and the promise is no longer mentioned.
- The approaches switch between affection, guilt and anger depending on which gets a reply.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They back off when you say you do not want contact.
- Evidence of change comes before any request. That could be treatment, steady work on the problem, or months of consistent behavior.
- The reason for contact is practical and specific, and ends once handled.
- They admit what went wrong in plain terms and do not ask you to forget it.
- You decide freely whether and when to respond, and nothing is lost if you do not.
- They stop when asked and do not send others in their place.
- Any change they describe is already visible in their actions over a long time.
- The reason for contact is practical and finishes when the task does.

## Love Bombing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/love-bombing

Someone showers you with love, praise and big promises far faster than they could really know you. Later the warmth turns out to come with strings.

Safety: Rapid intensity becomes a safety concern when it comes with pressure to cut off friends, share a home or money, or hand over passwords. It is also a concern when your no is met with anger or threats. Keep your own housing, income and phone access in place early on. Talk to a domestic abuse advocate if anything starts to feel like you cannot say no safely.

Signs it might be this:
- The affection arrives in a rush, then drops sharply after you commit, relax or push back on the pace.
- Your attempts to slow down are met with hurt, sulking or the suggestion that you do not feel as deeply as they do.
- The praise is generic enough that it could be said to anyone, and it does not change as they learn who you are.
- Gifts or sacrifices are mentioned later as a debt you owe.
- Your time with friends, family or work quietly shrinks because the contact is so constant.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can say 'I need to go slower' and the answer is a calm 'okay, thanks for telling me'.
- The warmth stays roughly the same through arguments, bad weeks and ordinary boredom.
- Their compliments are about particular things you have actually done or said.
- Your friendships, hobbies and sleep are intact and they ask about them with interest.
- They are equally open about their own flaws and do not treat you as flawless.
- You both feel carried along at about the same speed and can talk about it.
- Asking for space produces understanding rather than a visible drop in warmth.
- The relationship stays steady after the first wave of excitement fades.

## Manufactured Intimacy

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/manufactured-intimacy
Also called: Premature Vulnerability, Weaponized AI Empathy

Someone shares deep things, even serious pain, very fast. You end up feeling close to, and responsible for, a person you barely know.

Safety: Fast closeness alone is not a danger sign. Take it more seriously when it comes with pressure to hide the relationship, or to give money or housing. Also take it more seriously when you are told you are responsible for someone's life. If someone says they may hurt themselves, do not carry that alone. Contact a crisis line or emergency services for them, and tell a trusted person.

Signs it might be this:
- The depth of what has been shared is far greater than the number of times you have actually met.
- Confidences come with an unspoken invoice: you are expected to match them with equal depth soon.
- You feel obliged to protect or stay loyal to someone before you have seen them handle any real friction.
- Slowing the pace is treated as coldness, distrust or proof that you do not care.
- Disclosures sharpen at the moments you seem busy, doubtful or less available.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They are fine with you sharing less than they do, and they do not keep score.
- Their openness is the same with everyone in the room, not tuned to you.
- When you say you would like to go slower, they say 'of course' and nothing in their warmth changes.
- They asked whether you had room to listen before telling you something heavy.
- The closeness has grown steadily, with behavior that matches the words.
- They share at a pace they are happy to see you match, or not match, without any change in tone.
- They have friends, family or a counselor, and they ask about your life too.
- You can still keep other friendships and routines without anyone minding.

## Future Faking

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/future-faking
Also called: Paper Deferral

Someone describes a wonderful future with you in detail, so you keep waiting and putting up with the present. The promises keep sliding away.

Signs it might be this:
- The promised date has moved more than once, each time with a new explanation.
- There are no visible steps toward the promise, only talk about it.
- The promise comes up most when you voice doubt, complain or talk about leaving.
- You are being asked to give up something real now, such as time, money or an opportunity, on the strength of it.
- Small commitments today, like returning a call or showing up on time, are also not kept.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can see real progress, like savings accounts opened, applications filed, or treatment attended.
- They tell you plainly when a plan has slipped and what that means for you.
- You are not asked to put anything on hold while waiting.
- They are open to you deciding not to wait and do not use the promise to discourage this.
- Outside events that anyone could verify explain the delay.
- The delay has a real, checkable cause and you were told promptly.
- Concrete steps are happening in view, alongside the talk.
- You are free to make your own plans without being talked out of them.

## Manufactured Destiny

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/manufactured-destiny

Someone tells you the two of you are meant to be. Each time you hesitate, they use that story to make stepping back look like a mistake you can't undo.

Signs it might be this:
- The fate story gets louder specifically when you say you are unsure or want more time.
- Your hesitation is answered with a sign, a coincidence or a prophecy instead of a conversation.
- You are told that leaving would defy something larger, and you notice you feel afraid of the idea.
- The 'meant to be' claim arrived within days or weeks, before there was evidence either way.
- Practical concerns, such as differences in values or past hurts, are waved away as small in light of destiny.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They use the language only when things feel good, and drop it, calmly, when you want to talk through problems.
- They say it of other relationships in their life and apply it to friends and family too.
- When you say you want to slow down, they say 'okay' and the connection is unchanged.
- They treat the belief as theirs, and do not require you to share it.
- The sentiment is mutual and you use it yourself without feeling pressed.
- The language is warm and occasional, and it comes without any request that you stay.
- They are as comfortable with your doubts as with your certainty.
- Other people in their life describe them as sentimental or spiritual in general.

## Exclusive Meaning

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/exclusive-meaning
Also called: Exclusive Access, Privileged Access Framing

One person keeps telling you that nobody else gets you the way they do. Over time your friends and family start to feel like they do not count.

Safety: Narrowing the people you confide in can be an early part of coercive control. That is a pattern of rules and checking that slowly limits your life. It is most likely when it comes with checking your phone, deciding who you see, or anger when you make plans. Keep at least one outside contact who knows your real situation. If you are afraid of the reaction, call a domestic violence hotline to talk through options privately.

Signs it might be this:
- The remarks about being the only one who gets you come with remarks about specific people who supposedly do not.
- You notice you are sharing less with friends because they 'would not see it', in the other person's words.
- Your outside relationships are described as threats, competitors or bad influences.
- Being understood by them starts to feel like something you must keep earning by staying close.
- When you mention a friend's support, the reply is flat, wounded or quickly redirected to themselves.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They encourage you to talk to other people, and are pleased when you feel supported elsewhere.
- Their praise for your closeness is a fact about a moment, not a claim that rivals cannot compare.
- They speak well of your friends, and ask after them.
- You still bring different things to different people and none of it feels guarded.
- Their comments about someone in your life are specific and based on something that happened. They are not a general verdict.
- They are glad when you have other sources of comfort and make room for them.
- Compliments about understanding you do not come with criticism of anyone else.
- You can disagree with their reading of you and the conversation stays friendly.

## Pedestal Ploy / The Exception Script

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/pedestal-ploy-the-exception-script
Also called: Pedestal Ploy, The Exception Script, Social Elevation, The Exception Script (Recycled)

Someone praises you by putting down everyone else in your life. Slowly, being special to them starts to mean being cut off from the people who know you best.

Safety: Someone with power over you may single you out and ask for secrecy, gifts, private messaging or time alone. This is most worrying when an adult does it to a young person. That can be a warning sign of grooming or exploitation. Watch also for anger when you see friends, or checking of your messages or money. Tell a parent, school counselor or other trusted adult, or a domestic abuse advocate, before the secret grows.

Signs it might be this:
- The compliment depends on others looking worse.
- You are asked to keep the praise or the relationship secret from peers or family.
- Warmth drops noticeably after you spend time with, or take the side of, someone in your circle.
- The speaker's comments about your peers have become sharper since you got close.
- You find yourself pulling away from people who used to matter to you, feeling above them.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The praise is about specific work and could be repeated in front of everyone.
- They encourage you to include your peers and mention their strengths too.
- You can disagree with them and still be valued.
- The attention is open, such as a public award, and open to question by others.
- Where they criticize someone, they give a reason and do not require you to agree.
- The praise is public, specific and offered to others who earn it too.
- You are encouraged to bring your peers along and keep your friendships.
- You can question them without a drop in regard.

## Premature Vulnerability / Trauma Dumping

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/premature-vulnerability-trauma-dumping
Also called: Premature Vulnerability, Selective Vulnerability, floodlighting

Premature Vulnerability, sometimes called trauma dumping or Selective Vulnerability, is a very deep disclosure offered very early, before the relationship can carry it. A new partner, colleague, friend, leader or group member shares a painful history, a loss or a secret wound within days or hours.

Signs it might be this:
- You feel a duty of care toward someone you have known only briefly, and you cannot remember agreeing to it.
- Their disclosures come right before a request, or right after you set a limit.
- Criticism of what they do, at work or in the group, is met with a reminder of what they have been through.
- They seem to know little about you and show little interest, though they have told you a great deal.
- Other people describe being told the same story early on, followed by the same kind of request.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They shared once, then let the subject rest and did not bring it back as a reason you owe them anything.
- They are as interested in your life as in telling their own.
- They accept no without bringing up their pain.
- They have other support, such as friends, family or a professional, and do not cast you as the only one.
- The setting invited the disclosure, such as a grief group or a talk you asked for.
- The sharing slows down as the relationship finds its own pace.
- They check whether it is okay to tell you hard things, and accept it if it is not.
- Their story never comes back as a reason you should do or accept something.

## The Rescue Hook

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/the-rescue-hook

Someone seems unable to cope, and you step in without being asked. Over time you do a large share of their life, and it is called caring.

Signs it might be this:
- They struggle with tasks around you that they handle well at work or with other people.
- Offers to step back are met with distress, guilt or a drop in warmth.
- You feel you are doing things because you cannot bear to watch, not because anyone asked.
- There is little sign of learning the skill or reducing the dependence over time.
- Your own commitments, rest and plans are routinely moved aside for their emergencies.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They ask clearly for specific help and accept a 'no' without fuss.
- They are working on the skill or have a plan to need you less.
- The struggle is real, visible to others and consistent in every setting.
- They offer help back, in ways that matter to you, when you need it.
- They thank you without implying you owe them more.
- The need is stated plainly and they accept refusals without distress.
- There is visible progress or a plan to rely on you less over time.

## Emotional Parasitism

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/emotional-parasitism
Also called: Emotional Labor Extraction

You give most of the listening, comfort and energy, and they give little back. Over months or years you grow tired in a way that rest does not fix.

Signs it might be this:
- When you share your own troubles, they are quickly steered back to theirs.
- You feel more drained than uplifted after most of your contact with them.
- Over a year or more, you cannot recall a time they showed up for you in a comparable way.
- Naming the imbalance is met with hurt, defensiveness or a new crisis.
- You find yourself avoiding their calls, or saving energy for them in advance.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They checked in with you after a hard stretch of their own had passed.
- They remember what you told them and ask about it later.
- The current imbalance has a clear cause, such as a bereavement or illness, and is changing.
- They thank you and look for other supports as well.
- You get things from the friendship that matter to you, such as laughter, history or shared work.
- The imbalance has a clear cause that is easing, and they have begun to give back.
- When you name it, they listen and change something.
- You have other relationships where the giving and receiving feel fair.

## Pocketing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/pocketing
Also called: Stashing

Pocketing, also called Stashing, keeps you apart from the other person's friends, family and public life, so that the relationship exists only in private, with no witnesses. It is an informal term from dating culture and is best treated as a description, not a diagnosis.

Safety: If an adult is keeping a private relationship with a child or young person away from their family or school, treat it as a safeguarding concern and contact a safeguarding lead, a child protection service or the police; do not confront the adult yourself. If secrecy is part of wider control or you feel unsafe, a domestic abuse service or a crisis line can help you plan safely. In an emergency, call emergency services.

Signs it might be this:
- Months pass and the reasons for not meeting anyone keep changing.
- You find they have told others they are single or have not mentioned you.
- They become uncomfortable or annoyed when you are seen together.
- Your requests to meet their circle are treated as pressure or neediness.
- The secrecy suits them in ways that seem to keep options open.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You have agreed to the privacy together and both understand why.
- They show willingness to include you, even if slowly.
- There is a clear safety or cultural reason, and they talk about it openly.
- They are private with everyone, not just with you.
- You already meet some of their people, just not all yet.
- The privacy is mutual and agreed.
- They make gradual steps to include you.
- There is an honest reason, and you feel respected rather than hidden.

## Bread-crumbing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/bread-crumbing
Also called: Benching, Breadcrumbing, Cushioning, Hope as a Leash, stringing someone along

Someone sends you tiny scraps of attention now and then, enough to keep you waiting. But it never turns into a date, a plan or a real relationship.

Signs it might be this:
- Over months, nothing becomes a plan, even though warm words keep arriving.
- Contact picks up when you seem to be losing interest or seeing someone else.
- You are the only one proposing times, and your proposals get vague replies.
- When you ask where this is going, you get a compliment or a change of subject.
- You feel more hopeful after each message and more empty a day later.

Signs it is probably something else:
- When you suggest a date, they pick one and show up.
- They have said clearly what they can offer, and you are choosing to accept that.
- The gaps match their life, such as exams, shifts, or a sick relative.
- They also make effort to reach you, with real questions and follow-up.
- You never actually asked for more, so they may not know you want it.
- A direct question about plans gets a real answer, even if it is a no.
- Both of you know the contact is casual and are content with that.
- Their attention is steady in small ways and matches how they treat other friends.

## Ghosting as Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/ghosting-as-control
Also called: Ghosting-Orbiting Cycle, Ghost Discard

Someone vanishes without a word, leaves you guessing, and then turns up again just when you have started to put it behind you.

Signs it might be this:
- The silence began suddenly after a long run of steady, warm contact.
- Direct questions about what happened go unanswered, though the person is plainly active elsewhere.
- Messages come back soon after you mention a new job, a new relationship or a decision to move on.
- When they return, the gap is never acknowledged, and your questions about it are brushed aside.
- The cycle of vanishing and returning has happened more than once, with similar timing.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They gave a reason, even a brief or clumsy one, such as needing space or being overwhelmed.
- They are quiet with everyone in their life, and friends report the same.
- They come back and say what happened and own the gap without being asked.
- A clear event, like illness, travel or a lost phone, accounts for the quiet.
- The contact was only ever occasional, so this silence is closer to its usual rhythm than a break.
- The silence lasted days rather than months, and an explanation came when it ended.
- It was a one-off, and the friendship or relationship carried on at its usual pace afterward.
- Their habit of avoiding conflict is open and familiar, and you have seen it with other people too.

Sources:
- LeFebvre et al. (2019). Ghosting in Emerging Adults’ Romantic Relationships: The Digital Dissolution Disappearance Strategy. Imagination, Cognition and Personality. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1177/0276236618820519

## Trauma Bonding

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/trauma-bonding

You feel most attached to the person right after they hurt you. The same person who caused the pain is the one who comforts you.

Safety: This pattern can come with physical violence, threats, stalking, and control over money or contact. The days around leaving are often the riskiest. Watch for escalation, strangulation, threats to kill or to harm children or pets, and weapons. Ask a domestic violence advocate to help you build a leaving plan. It can include where your documents, a spare phone and a go-bag will be kept.

Signs it might be this:
- The reconciliations after bad episodes feel like the most intense moments of the relationship.
- You find yourself defending the person to friends while also being afraid of them.
- The same kind of harm returns, and the same kind of comfort follows it.
- Leaving brings a sharp physical longing, even though you know how things have been.
- The person who hurt you is the only one you want when you are upset.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The hard moments are honestly acknowledged and the behavior changes afterwards.
- Comfort and support come from several people besides the one involved in the conflict.
- The hurtful incidents were few, real repair followed, and months have passed without a repeat.
- Your feelings of closeness are steady and do not spike after conflict.
- You feel free to leave a conversation or a room without being afraid of what follows.
- Harm has stopped, and the closeness has remained steady without needing a crisis.
- You have other people you turn to for comfort, and you do turn to them.
- The person has acknowledged specific hurts and shown lasting change.

Sources:
- Dutton and Painter (1993). Emotional Attachments in Abusive Relationships: A Test of Traumatic Bonding Theory. Violence and Victims. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1891/0886-6708.8.2.105
- Patrick Carnes (1997). The Betrayal Bond. (Popular book) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL2654209W

## Emotional Flooding

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/emotional-flooding
Also called: Intensity as Intimacy

Things move through such big highs and lows, so quickly, that you never get a calm moment to think. The intensity can feel like love, but it also keeps you from seeing clearly.

Signs it might be this:
- You cannot remember the last ordinary, quiet day together.
- Big declarations or commitments arrive faster than you have had time to get to know the person.
- Every attempt to slow down is met with hurt, panic or a new crisis.
- You often make decisions, such as moving in or sending money, in the middle of an emotional peak.
- You feel exhausted, as well as swept up.

Signs it is probably something else:
- There are calm stretches, and the relationship is fine in them.
- Slowing down, when you ask, is accepted without punishment.
- The intensity matches something real going on in their life and eases when it passes.
- Decisions get made on ordinary days as well as at emotional peaks.
- You feel energized and clear-headed in the relationship, and not drained.
- You can slow things down without being punished for it.
- The intensity belongs to a clear, passing event.

## Identity Auditing

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/identity-auditing
Also called: Vulnerability Identification

Identity Auditing, also called Vulnerability Identification, is the quiet mapping of another person's weak points for later use. It can look like close attention: remembering your fears, your family history, your money worries, your insecurities and what you most want.

Safety: If your fears, secrets or status are being used to threaten or control you, keep a private record and contact a specialist support service, or the police if you are in danger. If an adult seems to be studying a child's loneliness or home life and building secret closeness, tell a trusted adult or a child protection service. Where immigration status or legal records are involved, seek qualified legal advice.

Signs it might be this:
- Things you shared in confidence come back at moments of conflict, pressure or persuasion.
- You feel someone knows exactly which buttons to press, and presses them when they want something.
- Their interest in your weak spots is far greater than their interest in your strengths or joys.
- You find out they have been asking others about your history or problems.
- You do not know what is recorded about you, or who uses it.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Their knowledge of your weak spots shows up as gentleness, not pressure.
- They tell you what they keep, and why, and let you correct or limit it.
- They have never used something you shared against you.
- The questions are as much about your hopes and interests as your fears.
- A single sharp remark was regretted and not repeated.
- Their knowledge is used to make things easier for you.
- You can ask to see records and get a clear answer.
- They respect it when you say a topic is off limits.

## Premature Trust Extraction

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/premature-trust-extraction

Premature Trust Extraction is pressure to share private things before the other person has earned the right to hold them. It might be a new partner, a leader, an app, a recruiter, a form or an institution asking about your fears, history, money, health or family very early.

Safety: If someone is pressing a child or young person to share private things or keep secrets with an adult, tell a trusted adult or contact a child protection service. Never share passwords, bank details or identity documents under pressure. If information is being used to threaten you, keep a record and contact the police or a specialist support service. If immigration status is involved, seek qualified legal advice before you share more.

Signs it might be this:
- You feel you have to share more than you want in order to be accepted or believed.
- Hesitation is treated as a problem with you, not as a normal choice.
- You cannot get a clear answer about who will see what you share, or for how long.
- The person or group shares little about themselves while collecting a lot about you.
- Things you shared early later come back in a way you did not expect.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The reason for the question is clear, and you can say no without cost.
- The asker explains confidentiality and its limits before you share.
- Sharing is two-way and grows slowly over time.
- The setting is one where personal detail is truly required, such as a medical visit, and it is handled with care.
- A single curious question was asked and dropped when you deflected.
- Declining is respected, and the relationship carries on warmly.
- The purpose, use and privacy of the information are clear before you share.
- Trust is built through what the other person does, not just what they ask.

## Gatekeeper Grooming

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/gatekeeper-grooming
Also called: Grooming the Environment

Gatekeeper Grooming, also called Grooming the Environment, is when the people around a target are won over first, so that later access goes unquestioned and concerns are not believed. The gatekeepers might be parents, partners, colleagues, managers, a congregation or a whole institution.

Safety: If you think a child or vulnerable person is at risk, contact a child protection or adult safeguarding service, or the police if there is immediate danger. Do not confront the person or question the child in detail yourself; leave that to trained professionals. If you are a child or young person and feel uneasy about an adult, tell a trusted adult or a child helpline. You will not be in trouble.

Signs it might be this:
- The person seems keen to win over the people who decide about access, more than the person they will spend time with.
- They offer help that creates time alone with someone, especially a child or a vulnerable adult.
- They ask for exceptions to normal rules and get them because people like them.
- When you feel uneasy, the people around you defend them before listening to you.
- The person seems to know in advance that you might not be believed.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They follow the same rules as everyone else and are happy with checks.
- Their help does not involve being alone with anyone.
- They respond calmly when someone asks a question about them.
- Gatekeepers still listen to concerns and take them seriously.
- The relationship is open, and everyone involved knows what is happening.
- Rules, checks and supervision apply to the person like anyone else.
- Concerns are welcomed and looked into, not dismissed.
- The person never seeks time alone with those they have power over.

## Target Selection

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/target-selection
Also called: Talent Identification and Institutional Capture

Target Selection is when one person is singled out for special attention because they look most isolated, most eager or most useful, and the attention feels like being chosen. It can happen in a family, a team, a workplace, a faith group, an online space or a school.

Safety: If you are a child or young person and an adult is giving you special attention, gifts or secrets, tell a trusted adult or contact a child helpline. If you are worried about a child, contact a child protection service, or the police if they are in immediate danger. Adults being targeted for money, sex or isolation can contact a specialist support service, or emergency services if in danger. Do not confront the person alone.

Signs it might be this:
- The attention feels intense, sudden and focused only on you.
- You are encouraged to keep the closeness, the gifts or the time private.
- You are the one with the fewest people looking out for you, and that seems to be part of why.
- Others in the group are treated very differently, or you are set apart from them.
- The attention starts to come with requests, tests of loyalty or a sense that you owe something.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The attention is open, and other people know about and support it.
- The person also helps others, not only you.
- Your other relationships are encouraged, not crowded out.
- There are no secrets, gifts with strings or one-to-one meetings out of view.
- The relationship is between equals with no power gap.
- The attention happens in the open, within normal roles and rules.
- Others are told, invited and involved.
- You can say no, step back or tell anyone without fear.

## Pacing and Leading

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/pacing-and-leading

Pacing and Leading is first matching another person's rhythm, mood, words and views, then gradually shifting them toward dependence. At the start, the person or group agrees with you, mirrors your tone and supports your plans.

Safety: A gradual shift toward dependence can be part of coercive control or grooming. If your money, movement, contact with others or health choices are being controlled, contact a specialist support service, or emergency services if you are in danger. If an adult seems to be slowly changing a child's boundaries or building secrecy, tell a trusted adult or a child protection service.

Signs it might be this:
- Looking back, the early agreement seems too complete to have been real.
- You now check with this person on decisions you used to make alone.
- Disagreeing with them now feels much harder than it did at the start.
- Your other relationships or sources of advice have quietly become less important.
- When you list the changes, they all point toward more reliance on one person or group.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The changes have made you more able and confident.
- You can disagree, and the warmth stays.
- The other person also adjusts to you, not only the other way round.
- The shift was discussed openly and you agreed to it.
- You still make important choices on your own.
- The guidance moves you toward independence.
- You can say no to a suggestion and nothing changes in the relationship.
- The person is open about what they are suggesting and why.

## Mirroring-on-Demand

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/mirroring-on-demand
Also called: Mirroring, Rapport Hijacking

A person seems to share everything you like and believe, so you sense a perfect match. The sameness changes shape depending on what you tell them.

Signs it might be this:
- Their stated interests have no earlier trace: no old posts, belongings, stories or friends who recognize them.
- Their opinions line up with yours on topics where most people disagree with each other.
- When you change a view, their view moves to match within days.
- They never disagree with you, even about small things, and bristle or sulk if you disagree with them.
- Friends who have seen them with other people say they seem like a different person.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They can say where an interest came from and show something done about it before you met.
- They disagree with you now and then, mildly, about things that matter to them.
- Their shared tastes were obvious from the start, such as a club you both joined for the same reason.
- Their way of speaking stays the same around other people.
- Their agreement is general warmth toward everybody, not tuned to you.
- Differences between you appear over time and are handled with interest rather than hurt.
- Their interests can be traced to something they did before they knew you.
- People who know them in other settings describe the same person you know.

## Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/idealize-devalue-discard-cycle

At first you are treated as perfect, then slowly as a disappointment. Then you are cast aside, as if the person you were praised for being no longer exists.

Signs it might be this:
- The early praise was extreme and fast, and it now reads as a script you were handed.
- The turn does not follow any event, and the criticism seems to be about who you are.
- Qualities they loved are now listed as flaws.
- You are compared with a partner they once idealized in the same words.
- The end arrives with little discussion, such as being blocked or ghosted.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The cooling follows a specific, nameable event that either of you could discuss.
- They still show care and respect while saying the relationship isn't working.
- You can both describe what changed, and the descriptions roughly match.
- Their past relationships ended for varied reasons with no repeated arc.
- The ending came with a conversation, even a hard one.
- Both of you can describe the relationship's rise and decline in similar terms.
- The criticism is specific and about behavior, not about your worth.

## Splitting

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/splitting
Also called: Splitting (Induced)

Someone puts you on a pedestal, then drops you to the bottom after something small. The swing seems to have little to do with what you did.

Signs it might be this:
- The same person has been called wonderful and worthless within the same year.
- What triggers the flip is trivial, such as a delay or a differing opinion.
- Past good events are redescribed as fake or forgotten once the view turns.
- Several people in their life describe the same swings.
- Reassurance and evidence do not move the new view until it flips back by itself.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The change followed something serious that you can name.
- They can still say good things about the person they are upset with.
- Their view of others changes slowly and for stated reasons.
- After a cooling-off period they can describe both the problem and what they value.
- Other reasonable people who saw the same events hold the same view.
- The flip followed an actual breach and is proportionate to it.
- They can hold both the good and the problem in view once the first heat passes.
- The swings are rare, and you have been able to talk about them afterward.

## Confirmation Bias Exploitation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/confirmation-bias-exploitation

After something painful, they are lovely for a while. You hold on to that as the real them and explain away the painful moments.

Signs it might be this:
- Warm periods follow incidents with a regularity you could predict.
- Telling a friend about the incident you notice yourself softening it as you speak.
- You keep the good memories close to hand specifically for the moments you doubt.
- Raising the harm brings a list of what the person has done for you, instead of a response to what happened.
- The kind periods change what is said but not what is done about the cause of the harm.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The kindness is steady and does not rise and fall around incidents.
- After a bad moment, the person names what went wrong and the cause is dealt with.
- You feel free to describe the incident to anyone without feeling disloyal.
- The harm was one event, long ago, and has not returned.
- Your doubts get answered and then settle, rather than returning after each sweet spell.
- The good periods continue without interruption and the harmful incidents grow rarer.
- The person helps you look at what happened and does not need you to forgive it quickly.
- You can discuss the hard moments with people close to you without defending the person.

Sources:
- Nickerson (1998). Confirmation Bias: A Ubiquitous Phenomenon in Many Guises. Review of General Psychology. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1037/1089-2680.2.2.175

## Premature Exclusivity

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/premature-exclusivity

Someone asks you to be exclusive far sooner than you can know them. If you want more time, they answer with hurt or pressure instead of patience.

Signs it might be this:
- Your request for more time brings sulking, accusations, or sudden coldness.
- A deadline is attached to the question of commitment.
- You are asked to end other friendships or contacts before you know the person well.
- Declarations of how special you are arrive in a rush, and doubt is treated as an insult to them.
- You noticed you agreed mainly to end an uncomfortable conversation.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You raised the pace yourself, or you are as keen as they are.
- When you ask for time, they say 'okay, take it' and keep seeing you the same way.
- The commitment requested is small and easy to revisit, like deleting an app together.
- Both of you agreed on the pace afterwards and neither of you feels cornered.
- They tell you early and plainly what they want and leave the choice open.
- A request for time is met warmly and the relationship carries on at your pace.
- The person has been open from the start about what they want and has not asked you to shrink the rest of your life.
- Both of you can say the pace is too fast or too slow and the other one adjusts.

## Orbiting

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/orbiting

Orbiting is when someone who has ended contact, or been distanced, keeps watching from a distance in a way that keeps them present in the other person's mind. A former partner stops replying but still views every story and likes old photos.

Signs it might be this:
- They ended contact or stopped replying, yet keep visibly watching what you post.
- Their reactions seem timed to moments when you are moving on, such as a new relationship.
- Asking them what they want gets no answer, but the watching continues.
- You notice you post or check things with them in mind.
- They resurface briefly, then go silent again, without ever talking things through.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The ending was friendly and you both agreed to stay connected.
- Their activity is rare, ordinary and matches how they treat everyone else.
- They reply when you message and are open about wanting contact or not.
- You are the one checking their activity, and they are not doing anything new.
- There is a shared reason for contact, such as children or a joint project.
- Their activity is rare and fits how they behave with everyone.
- They respect it if you block, mute or say you want no contact.
- You feel neutral, not hooked, when you see it.

## Rescuer Positioning

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/rescuer-positioning
Also called: Leadership Arrival Narrative

Rescuer Positioning is presenting oneself as the answer to another person's confusion or fear. A partner, mentor, leader, salesperson, group or institution arrives at a hard moment and offers certainty: 'I know what to do, and I'm the one who can get you through.' In a group or workplace it can take the shape of a Leadership Arrival Narrative, where a new leader is cast as the one who will save everyone from chaos.

Safety: If a rescuer controls your money, home, documents, medication or contact with others, you may be in a controlling situation. Contact a specialist support service, or emergency services if you are in danger. If an adult positions themselves as a child's only safe person and asks for secrecy, tell a trusted adult or a child protection service. For health or legal fears, check with a qualified doctor or legal adviser.

Signs it might be this:
- The help seems to make you more dependent, not more able.
- The rescuer speaks badly of your other supports, or discourages you from getting a second opinion.
- The danger or confusion seems to grow whenever you think about managing without them.
- Their help is framed as the only option, with no alternatives mentioned.
- Doubting them is treated as a betrayal of everything they have done for you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They point you to other help and encourage you to use it.
- They are pleased when you need them less.
- They are clear about the limits of what they can do.
- You can say no to their help and they stay kind.
- The fear was real and the help truly resolved it.
- The help has a clear end point, and you are moving toward it.
- They are open about costs, limits and alternatives.
- Your other relationships and supports grow stronger, not weaker.

## Identity Hooking

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/identity-hooking
Also called: Identity Installation, Social Identity Threat

Someone insists that who you are and what you have achieved are really theirs, so that moving on from them feels like erasing yourself.

Signs it might be this:
- The claim of ownership comes up mainly when you mention leaving, a new opportunity, or a bigger life.
- Your achievements get retold as the other person's achievements, even in front of others.
- Thanking them is never enough; the debt is described as total and permanent.
- Your own part in what you have done is waved away as luck or as something they handed you.
- You catch yourself downplaying your wins around them to avoid the speech about who made you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They are glad about your plans and the credit they mention stays in proportion to what they did.
- The comment about their role came once, with visible hurt, and was followed by a plain 'it is your life'.
- You are the one who feels obliged, and nobody has told you that you are.
- They ask for something specific in return, such as help for a few weeks, rather than claiming your identity.
- Others who were there confirm the help was real, and nobody is using it as a leash.
- The credit claimed is proportionate and sits beside real acknowledgment of your own effort.
- Your plans for independence are met with mixed feelings but no claim over you.
- The topic comes up occasionally in a warm voice and never as a condition.

## Replacement Display

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/replacement-display

Replacement Display is publicly showcasing your replacement in a way that signals you are disposable. A new partner is paraded on social media soon after a breakup, a new hire is celebrated loudly in front of you, a new favorite student is praised in class, or a friendship group openly welcomes someone into the place you held.

Signs it might be this:
- The display happens very soon after you were pushed out.
- It appears in places or ways that seem chosen for you to see.
- Comparisons are made, openly or by hint, with you.
- Mutual contacts pass it on to you, or are encouraged to.
- It happens alongside other signs of being devalued or discarded.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The person is simply living their life and not addressing you.
- The new person was welcomed in an ordinary way.
- There are no comparisons or hints aimed at you.
- You can mute, block or step away and the display does not follow you.
- The timing has a clear ordinary reason, such as a planned start date.
- There is no comparison, no timing aimed at you, and no use of mutual contacts.
- You can easily mute or step away.
- The display is ordinary for the setting.

## Sudden Devaluation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/sudden-devaluation
Also called: Disposability Architecture

Sudden Devaluation is an abrupt shift from investment to disposal. A person, partner, employer, mentor, group or institution that once gave you warmth, attention and praise turns cold, dismissive or indifferent, often with little warning and no clear reason.

Signs it might be this:
- The change is sharp and fast, not gradual.
- It follows soon after you committed, signed, paid, moved or gave something important.
- No one will explain what changed, and asking is treated as needy or difficult.
- Things once praised are now treated as faults.
- You find yourself working much harder for scraps of the old warmth.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The other person tells you what changed, even if it hurts.
- There is a clear outside reason, such as a crisis, an illness or a heavy workload.
- The change is gradual and mutual.
- They still treat you with basic respect, even with less closeness.
- Warmth returns after a hard period without you having to earn it.
- There is an honest explanation and basic respect continues.
- The change matches a clear outside event.
- You can talk about it and are heard.

## Shame Installation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/shame-installation
Also called: Shame Cycling

A mistake gets treated as proof that something is wrong with you as a person. In time, the shame stays with you even when the other person is not there.

Signs it might be this:
- The criticism moves from what you did to what you are.
- Old failures are listed as proof every time something new happens.
- There is no stated way to repair it, only more disappointment.
- After a conversation, you feel dirty or defective, as well as sorry.
- Ordinary needs or traits get treated as moral failings.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They say what was wrong, say what they'd like to see, and move on once it's done.
- The disapproval is about a real harm and you agree it was one.
- They put it in terms of the act, such as 'that was not okay'.
- They are equally hard on their own errors in the same moral language.
- You feel sorry and motivated to fix it, not diminished.
- They name the act, say how it affected them, and let it go once addressed.
- Your past errors are not used as ammunition in new disputes.
- You can disagree with them without being told you are a bad person.

## Comparative Devaluation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/comparative-devaluation
Also called: Averages as Benchmarks, Comparison Architecture, Comparison Weaponization, Positional Scoring, Ranking Architecture, Real-Time Visibility

Someone keeps pointing to other people who do things better, so you feel you are never quite enough, no matter what you do.

Signs it might be this:
- The comparison arrives when you have asked for something or raised a concern.
- The comparison figure changes but you always end up on the losing side.
- The praise for the other person is delivered in front of you.
- Your own improvements are not counted and the target moves.
- The comparison names a person rather than a behavior, so there is nothing specific to work on.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They describe the other person's action in a way you could copy and are glad when you do.
- The comparison is occasional and the same standards are applied to them.
- They also compare themselves unfavorably and are open about it.
- Your progress gets acknowledged when it happens.
- You asked for a model and they offered one.
- The comparison points to a specific action you could actually take.
- When you say it hurts, the comparisons stop.

## Negging

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/negging
Also called: Backhanded Compliments, Body Shaming (Covert)

Someone mixes small put-downs into their compliments. You end up feeling a bit worse about yourself and a bit more eager to win their approval.

Signs it might be this:
- The sting always lands on a tender spot you have mentioned or shown.
- The compliment only works if you accept a small insult with it.
- When you react, you are told you are too sensitive or cannot take a joke.
- You notice a pull to prove them wrong, followed by relief when they approve.
- The comments are mostly made in front of others, or when you were doing well.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They stop and apologize when you say a comment stung.
- They tease themselves in the same way.
- Their praise, when it comes, has no tag line.
- The same remark would have been fine from a friend of equal standing and you find it funny too.
- It happened once and has not come up again.
- The teasing flows both ways and is about a variety of subjects.
- You leave most conversations feeling at least as good about yourself as when you arrived.

## Name-Calling Disguised as Humor

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/name-calling-disguised-as-humor
Also called: Sarcasm as Weapon, Humor as Weapon, disparagement humour, just joking

Someone says something insulting and wraps it in 'just kidding', so if you are hurt, you become the person who cannot take a joke.

Signs it might be this:
- The jokes land on one person and rarely on the speaker.
- The word or label would sound like an insult if you took the laugh away.
- You have asked them to stop and the same line came back within days.
- You laugh along in public and feel sick afterwards.
- Your hurt is answered with a comment about your sense of humor.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They stop at once when you say it stung and check that you are okay.
- You make jokes about them too and they laugh in the same way.
- The teasing is about shared, light things, not your sore spots.
- You find yourself actually laughing, and you are not performing laughter.
- A third person who knows you both would call the dynamic even.
- Both of you tease and either can call a stop.
- The joke ends the moment you say you did not like it.
- The subject is something you are comfortable with and have joked about yourself.

## Contempt

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/contempt
Also called: Curiosity Dismissal, Intellectual Belittling, Microexpressions of Contempt, Projected Disgust

Contempt is when someone looks down on you with disgust, so the message is not 'that was wrong' but 'you are beneath me'.

Signs it might be this:
- The scorn is about what you are, such as your intelligence, body, family or upbringing, and not about a particular action.
- Facial expressions and sighs do the work, so you often cannot quote the thing that stung.
- It appears in ordinary moments, like how you load a dishwasher, as well as in big disputes.
- You are talked about with an audience in mind, so others laugh or look away.
- Raising it gets a further eye-roll or a remark that you are being pathetic about this too.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The harsh words are about one clear act and are dropped once it is discussed.
- They are as hard on themselves as on you and use the same sneering voice about their own errors.
- The sarcasm is mutual and you both enjoy it.
- It happened during an acute crisis such as grief or sleeplessness and has not repeated since.
- They can state the thing they respect in you without strain, and mean it.
- The scorn is rare and tied to a specific moment, and they own it afterwards.
- You can do the same, return fire and be met with laughter and not offense.
- Disagreements usually stay aimed at the issue rather than at your character.

Sources:
- John Mordechai Gottman (1993). What Predicts Divorce?. (Research) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1982055W

## Performative Public Affection / Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/performative-public-affection-dr-jekyll-and-mr-hyde
Also called: Performative Public Affection, Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde, Charm Offensive, Dr. Jekyll / Mr. Hyde, Public Praise / Private Punishment

Everyone outside the home sees a kind, attentive person. Alone with you, they are cold, controlling or cruel. Because no one else sees it, you wonder who will believe you.

Safety: A split like this can sit alongside controlling behavior, threats, or physical harm that stays hidden from outsiders. Warning signs are fear of what happens after guests go home, or being told you would not be believed. Another is having your phone, money or contacts checked. Tell a domestic abuse advocate first. Keep your records somewhere private and out of the home.

Signs it might be this:
- How they treat you when others are around is so different that you are unsure which one is real.
- The hostile side shows up only where nobody else would see or hear it.
- Friends or relatives have said they find the person lovely, and you have stopped bringing it up.
- The kindness shows up after the harshness, in a way that makes you doubt your memory of it.
- They have said, or you believe, that no one would take your word over theirs.

Signs it is probably something else:
- People close to you have also seen the harsh side and do not find your account surprising.
- The private behavior is irritable but not cruel, and gets owned and apologized for.
- The difference is one of volume or formality, such as being relaxed at home and polite at work.
- A specific, understandable conflict sits behind the tension, and both of you can talk about it.
- The warm public manner is also how they treat you when you are alone together.
- The difference is mostly in volume and formality, and nothing in private is hurtful.
- Hard moments in private are named and repaired afterward, and do not return in the same form.

## Ambient Abuse / Atmosphere Control

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/ambient-abuse-atmosphere-control
Also called: Ambient Abuse, Erosion Through Accumulation

There is no big fight to point to. It is the sighs, the sharp tone, and the need to guess the mood. You end up tired all the time and cannot say why.

Safety: A tense atmosphere can be the background to controlling behavior, including monitoring, money limits or fear of what a mood might lead to. Watch whether you are afraid of an outburst, change your behavior to prevent one, or feel unsafe saying no. A domestic abuse advocate can help you assess this. They do not need a dramatic incident to take it seriously.

Signs it might be this:
- You can feel the mood in the house the moment you open the door, and adjust your behavior before anything has been said.
- You cannot name an incident that explains your exhaustion, yet you feel worn out.
- The tension rises and falls with one person's moods, not with outside events.
- You've started avoiding being home, or being in the same room, without a specific reason.
- When you try to describe it, you hear yourself saying "it's nothing really" before listing it.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The tension has a clear outside source, such as a job loss, and eases when the source does.
- Everyone in the household feels it in the same way and says so openly.
- The mood is discussed and the other person tries to change it when asked.
- You feel at ease in most rooms and with most people, and the unease is limited to a short period.
- The sense of dread started with your own anxiety and eases when you have been reassured.
- The tension tracks a known stress and lifts when it passes.
- The people involved can talk about the mood and something changes afterward.
- You feel relaxed around others and your unease is tied to a particular stretch of time.

## Emotional Invalidation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/emotional-invalidation
Also called: Covert Invalidation, Delegitimizing Emotion

When you say how you feel, you get told you should not feel that way, so you stop saying it.

Signs it might be this:
- Your feeling is dismissed before the reason is heard.
- The same type of feeling, such as anger or worry, is always ruled out.
- Comfort comes with a lecture about why you should feel differently.
- You find yourself apologizing for being upset.
- The original problem never gets discussed, because the argument becomes about whether you are allowed to feel this way.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They listen first and then offer a different view.
- They say they do not get it but believe you.
- They are open about being too tired to take it in, and return to it later.
- They express similar views about their own feelings, being gentle with them.
- Your feeling is taken seriously even when they disagree about the cause.
- You get a similar reception to feelings you have on good days and bad.

## Baiting

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/baiting
Also called: Reactive Abuse Provocation

Someone pokes at you until you snap, then points to your reaction as proof that you are the problem.

Signs it might be this:
- A jab comes just before the blow-up, and the same jab has come before earlier ones.
- The first remark is quiet and deniable, and the second, your response, is the one that gets named.
- Your reaction is recorded, quoted, or brought to others while the jab is left out.
- They keep going after you say you are close to losing your temper.
- Afterward you are described as the unstable or aggressive one.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They apologize for their part and acknowledge what set you off.
- They try to calm things once they see you are upset.
- Both of you started it in turn and both can say so.
- The topic was something that had to be discussed and was raised clumsily.
- Their account of the exchange includes what they said.
- You both react, and both own it afterwards.
- The provocative remarks stop when you say they are making things worse.

## "You've Changed"

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/you-ve-changed

The words 'you've changed' can be a plain observation or a quiet accusation. As a tactic, they treat your growth, new views or new limits as proof that you have lost your true self.

Signs it might be this:
- The remark comes right after you set a limit or say no.
- Nobody asks why you changed, only complains that you did.
- Your new views are blamed on outside influences, such as a school, a city, a partner or a counselor, rather than credited to you.
- Warmth and belonging seem to be on offer only if you go back to how you were.
- Several people in the same circle begin using the same phrasing about you.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They are curious about the change and want to understand it.
- They name a specific behavior that hurt them, such as missed visits, rather than your whole self.
- They accept your answer even if they do not like it.
- The change they point to is one you are uneasy about too.
- It was said once, in a sad moment, and not used later to win arguments.
- They tell you what they miss and also what they like about the newer you.
- They are willing to try new ways of being close, such as different activities or times.
- Your limits are kept even while they are getting used to them.

## Emotional Contamination

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/emotional-contamination

Emotional Contamination is the habit of breaking into someone's good moment with something that spoils it. News of a promotion is met at once with a worry about money.

Signs it might be this:
- The topic could easily have waited a few hours or days, and nothing was gained by raising it then.
- Good moments in your life are, more often than not, the ones that end in tension with this person.
- The topic has no link to the occasion, such as an old complaint brought up during a toast.
- When you ask to talk about it later, they insist it has to be now.
- Your news is met with a problem, while their own news is expected to be celebrated.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The person had no way of knowing it was a special moment for you.
- The issue was time-sensitive and they acknowledged the bad timing.
- They usually share in your good moments, and this was a rare slip.
- They agreed easily when you asked to save it for later.
- The worry they raised was one you shared, and you were glad it came up.
- They notice the timing on their own and offer to come back to it.
- Your good news is usually welcomed, and the odd interruption is a clear exception.
- What they raised was real, specific and something you could act on.

## Exoticization

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/exoticization

Exoticization treats a culture or identity as something to look at rather than people to know. The person or group is welcome in costume, at a festival, as a dish or a dance, and is praised as colorful or mysterious.

Signs it might be this:
- Your background only comes up on festival days, food days or as a fun fact.
- You are asked to wear, cook or perform something, but rarely asked what you think.
- Remarks about your looks or manner tie them to being foreign or 'exotic'.
- Your community appears in materials only in traditional scenes, never in ordinary modern life.
- When you talk about everyday issues in your community, interest fades.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You were invited to lead and shape the event yourself.
- Interest in your culture comes alongside interest in you as an individual.
- Present-day people and realities are included as well as traditions.
- You can decline to share without losing standing.
- The person changes course when you say the framing feels narrow.
- The person listens when you describe ordinary life and treats it as just as interesting.
- The event is one of many ways the group includes you.
- Comments are about what you do, not about how unusual you seem.

## Public Exposure

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/public-exposure
Also called: Public Humiliation, Public Identification, Public Shaming

You are put down, corrected or laughed at, or something private is shown to others. It would have been handled differently one on one. The audience is what makes it hurt.

Safety: Humiliation is mostly about standing and dignity, but it can sit alongside danger. Watch for intimate images or private details shared without consent, or hints that something will be revealed unless you comply. Exposure that follows you from the household into work or online spaces is another sign. Save dated screenshots. Before replying, ask a legal aid service or an advocate who handles image-based or domestic abuse about next steps.

Signs it might be this:
- The criticism is harsher with people around than when you are alone together.
- Private things, such as a mistake, a diagnosis or a secret, are brought out in front of others.
- The same person is picked out in group settings more than anyone else is.
- A quiet word would have been easy to arrange and was never tried.
- Others glance at you or look away afterwards, and the room seems to settle on you as the joke.

Signs it is probably something else:
- The feedback is the same for everyone and given in a way that is meant to be useful.
- It was an emergency or a safety issue that needed fixing straight away.
- You agreed to the format, such as a review session where all work is critiqued.
- The speaker followed up privately to check how you felt and repaired it.
- The comment was clumsy but kind in tone, and the person was visibly sorry.
- Everyone is treated the same, and the setting makes public correction expected.
- The person speaks to you in private afterward and makes it right.
- The topic was a work task, and no personal detail was used.

## Dehumanization

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/dehumanization

A person is talked about or handled as a case, a number or a type, and no one seems to ask what they think.

Safety: Dehumanizing language can come with loss of choices, contact, money, housing or safety, especially where you depend on the people using it. Watch for being moved, restricted or medicated without explanation, or for threats tied to a label. Contact an independent advocate, ombudsman or legal aid service early, and tell someone outside the setting where you are.

Signs it might be this:
- You are referred to by a label, number or room, including in front of you.
- Decisions are made about you without asking you, or told to you after the fact.
- Your questions are answered by speaking to the person with you instead of to you.
- Others in the same setting are addressed by name and consulted, while you are not.
- Your complaints are treated as symptoms of your category.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Everyone in the setting gets the same formal process, and each person is still addressed by name.
- You are asked for your view before decisions, even in a hurry.
- Labels are used between professionals only, with explanations offered to you in ordinary words.
- The staff member is brusque with everyone, and apologized when you pointed it out.
- Procedures you find cold are required by law or policy, and someone is willing to explain them.
- The impersonal language is used for everyone and paired with courtesy.
- You are consulted before decisions and told what they mean.
- A staff member responds to being corrected about your name or role.

Sources:
- Bandura (1999). Moral Disengagement in the Perpetration of Inhumanities. Personality and Social Psychology Review. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr0303_3
- Haslam (2006). Dehumanization: An Integrative Review. Personality and Social Psychology Review. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr1003_4

## Objectification

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/objectification
Also called: Body Commodification

You matter to them for what you do or how you look, and when that is not needed, they seem to lose interest.

Signs it might be this:
- Contact falls away when you have nothing to offer, such as during illness, grief or a gap in your usefulness.
- People talk about you by your role or looks, not your name or views.
- Your opinions on matters outside your function get a blank response.
- When you decline to do the useful thing, the mood turns cold.
- You find that you are introduced by what you do for them.

Signs it is probably something else:
- They ask about your life and listen to the answer, including when you cannot help.
- The relationship is clearly a contract both sides chose and describe the same way.
- They notice when you are tired and let you off.
- Their focus on your skill appears only in a task setting.
- They would still be glad to see you if you stopped being useful.
- Both of you understand and agreed to a limited, functional relationship.
- They show curiosity about your life that is not tied to a need.

Sources:
- Fredrickson and Roberts (1997). Objectification Theory: Toward Understanding Women's Lived Experiences and Mental Health Risks. Psychology of Women Quarterly. (Research) https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1471-6402.1997.tb00108.x

## Conditional Love

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/conditional-love
Also called: Conditional Worth, Conditional Approval, Love as Performance Metric, Struggle Prohibition

Someone makes you feel that you matter only while you are helpful or agreeable, and that your place shrinks when you are not.

Signs it might be this:
- The warmth you get tracks what you did for them that week, and falls off when you rest or say no.
- Criticism of a missed task turns into a statement about your character.
- You are praised mainly when you are producing, serving or agreeing.
- Your needs, illness or tiredness are met with irritation instead of care.
- You catch yourself calculating what you have done lately to deserve kind treatment.

Signs it is probably something else:
- Disappointment about a task passes without affecting how you are treated afterward.
- You can be unproductive, ill or unhelpful for a while and still be welcomed without a price.
- The expectation is applied equally to everyone in the household or team, including the speaker.
- They thank you for help without making the thanks a precondition for friendliness.
- The standard is set by a role, such as an employer's job description, and not by a personal verdict.
- Standards are applied fairly to everyone and are tied to a role, not to personal worth.
- Care continues even when you are unhelpful, sick or in need.
- The remarks about usefulness are rare and are followed by warmth.

## Internalized Conditioning

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/internalized-conditioning

The rules of someone who once controlled the room now play inside your own head, so you police yourself even when they are gone.

Signs it might be this:
- You can name the person whose phrasing the inner voice uses.
- The penalty you brace for is one that person once handed out, though no one else in your life would.
- The rule switches on in settings that person never visits.
- Your preference and the rule point in opposite directions and the rule wins without a debate.
- Their absence brought less relief than you expected, and the rules sometimes feel louder.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can explain the rule's reasons in your own words and would pick it again.
- The voice sounds like a mentor whose advice you test and sometimes ignore.
- Breaking the rule leaves you uneasy for a minute, not dreading for days.
- The standard applies to everyone in your life and is not tied to one person's disapproval.
- It shows up only in a stressful stretch and fades when the stress does.
- The rule is one you have looked at and still endorse.
- It eases when you are rested, among people you trust, or far from old triggers.
- You can break it sometimes without a spike of dread.

## Pre-Punishment

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/pre-punishment

You turn yourself down before anyone else gets the chance. You do not apply, speak or try, because it once felt dangerous to be noticed, and not trying feels safer.

Signs it might be this:
- You pull back from things you want, before anyone has said no.
- The fear is specific: being noticed, laughed at, or held to a higher standard.
- You can trace the reflex to an earlier place or person where standing out cost you.
- The expected punishment is vivid, though you cannot point to anything like it happening in your present life.
- Relief comes when you stay out of it, followed by quiet regret.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You have weighed the odds and honestly decided it is not for you.
- You pass on things that do not interest you, and take up the ones that do.
- Your caution fits a real risk in your present situation.
- You turn down opportunities without distress, and do not later wish you had tried.
- The pullback is brief, tied to a hard stretch, and lifts when your circumstances improve.
- You can name a clear, current reason for holding back that you are comfortable with.
- You sometimes take the risk anyway, and it goes fine.
- You do not feel regret afterwards.

## Silence Installation

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/silence-installation

There are things you cannot make yourself say, because the earlier times you tried went badly. The silence is protection you learned, not weakness.

Safety: Silence alone is not a danger sign. It matters more when the topic you cannot raise involves being hurt, threatened, watched or kept short of money. Then the silence may be shielding you from a real risk. Many advocacy lines offer chat or text for people who cannot speak freely. Start there, at a time and place the person it concerns cannot see.

Signs it might be this:
- You can trace the freeze to a specific time when speaking up was punished or mocked.
- The block appears around the same person or topic even when you are calm.
- You rehearse again and again and still skip it when the moment comes.
- Others mention that you seem fine because you never raise anything, while you are not fine.
- The dread arrives before you have even decided whether the issue is worth raising.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You stay quiet for a few days, then bring it up on your own terms.
- You can say it to a friend or counselor, even if saying it to one particular person is hard.
- The reluctance is about choosing a good time and not about expecting consequences.
- The topic is simply private, and you are at peace with that.
- The freeze is part of a wider anxiety that appears in every setting, and a professional is already helping with it.
- Writing the message down, or saying it to a trusted listener, comes easily.
- The block loosens when circumstances change, such as a new setting or a calmer week.
- You choose silence on some topics and feel fine about the choice.

## Fawning

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/fawning

When someone feels scary, you switch into pleasing them: agreeing, saying sorry, hiding what you think. You learned it because it once kept you safe.

Signs it might be this:
- The urge to please is strongest around one person or type of situation that feels unsafe.
- There is a physical feel of dread or tightness just before you agree.
- You apologize in advance for things that are not your fault.
- You track their mood closely and adjust before they have said anything.
- You agree out loud while privately holding a different view, and cannot say why you did not speak.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You are accommodating because you care and feel free to say no to this person.
- The pleasing eases or disappears around people who feel safe.
- The agreement follows genuine reflection and you still hold it afterward.
- You feel neutral or warm, not afraid, when you go along with the group.
- The deference is part of a shared cultural custom you value.
- The pleasing is occasional, chosen and comes with an ability to say no.
- You go back to your own opinions easily once the moment passes.
- You feel at ease with most people and keep the habit for rare tense moments.

Sources:
- Pete Walker (2013). Complex PTSD. (Where the name comes from) https://openlibrary.org/works/OL19987839W

## Identity Erosion

URL: https://noblefathercreations.com/playbook/identity-erosion
Also called: Self-Abandonment

You look up and cannot say what you like, what you think or where your limits are. Most of it has been bent around keeping someone else content.

Safety: Watch for signs that the narrowing is being enforced and did not simply drift in. These include limits on friends, money, phone or travel, or days of anger or silence when you disagree. If any of that is present, a domestic abuse advocate can help you plan privately. You can choose a pace and a device that are safe for you. Do this before anything is raised with the other person.

Signs it might be this:
- You can name specific things you loved before the relationship that you now avoid or feel awkward about.
- You pre-check how a friend, hobby or opinion will be received before you act on it.
- You agree out loud with views you privately do not hold, mostly to avoid a bad reaction.
- Your own exhaustion, limits or wishes feel like problems to hide rather than information to use.
- Imagining a day entirely on your own leaves you unsure what you would do with it.

Signs it is probably something else:
- You can say why each change happened and would make the same choice again.
- Your old friends are still in your life, though you see them less because of distance.
- You have taken on your partner's hobby and still do things that only you enjoy.
